speaker: Unknown
en: Almost everyone living in a modern economy now is going to have hundreds of interactions with a phone or with a computer.
zh: 几乎每一个生活在现代经济体中的人，现在都将要经历数百次与手机或计算机的交互。

speaker: Unknown
en: And unfortunately, a lot of those interactions are not going to be great.
zh: 遗憾的是，这些交互中有很多并不会很棒。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have an obligation as product people to put that emotional energy back into people's lives.
zh: 作为产品人，我们有义务将那种情感能量重新注入人们的生活。

speaker: Unknown
en: You actually have a really unique perspective on just what is design.
zh: 对于究竟什么是设计，你确实有着真正独特的视角。

speaker: Unknown
en: Design is trying to imagine the future you want to live in and then take the steps to make it real.
zh: 设计就是试图想象你想要生活在其中的未来，然后采取措施使其成为现实。

speaker: Unknown
en: Saying a company is design-led does not mean it's designer-led.
zh: 说一家公司是以设计为主导的，并不意味着它是由设计师主导的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've never seen somebody graft it on after the fact.
zh: 我从未见过有人事后将其嫁接上去。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's there at the beginning in the root DNA or doesn't exist.
zh: 它从一开始就存在于根 DNA 中，否则就不存在。

speaker: Unknown
en: It wasn't a successful stint at Pinterest.
zh: 在 Pinterest 的那一段经历并不成功。

speaker: Unknown
en: I just bounced off the culture.
zh: 我只是与那里的文化格格不入。

speaker: Unknown
en: I came in thinking I was supposed to behave the way I behaved at Apple, which is very direct, fighting hard.
zh: 我进来时以为我应该像我在 Apple 时的那样行事，那是非常直接的、努力争取的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why did you decide to join Apple?
zh: 你为什么决定加入 Apple？

speaker: Unknown
en: I just seek out opportunities to witness history.
zh: 我只是寻求机会去见证历史。

speaker: Unknown
en: The whole company is constantly asking how can the thing that I'm working on be a little bit better?
zh: 整个公司都在不断在问，我正在做的事情怎么能变得更好一点？

speaker: Unknown
en: Why do you Think that people that have left Apple, a lot of amazing things haven't emerged?
zh: 你为什么认为那些离开了 Apple 的人，很多了不起的事情并没有涌现出来？

speaker: Unknown
en: Today, my guest is Bob Baxley.
zh: 今天，我的嘉宾是 Bob Baxley。

speaker: Unknown
en: Bob is a designer, executive and advisor who's built in led design teams at Apple, Pinterest, Yahoo, and most recently ThoughtSpot.
zh: Bob 是一位设计师、高管和顾问，他曾在 Apple、Pinterest、Yahoo 构建并领导设计团队，最近是在 ThoughtSpot。

speaker: Unknown
en: Over the course of his career that spanned over three decades, Bob has played a pivotal role in the design of the Apple online store, the Apple App Store, Pinterest, and early in his career Yahoo Answers, products that have been used by hundreds of millions of people around the world.
zh: 在他跨越三十多年的职业生涯中，Bob 在 Apple 线上商店、Apple App Store、Pinterest 的设计中发挥了关键作用，以及在他职业生涯早期的 Yahoo Answers，这些产品被全世界数以亿计的人使用。

speaker: Unknown
en: Bob also mentors individuals and advises organizations that are working to improve the practice, craft and culture of digital product design.
zh: Bob 还指导个人并咨询那些致力于改善数字产品设计实践、工艺和文化的组织。

speaker: Unknown
en: There is something in this conversation for everyone from why you should consider having designed report engineering, why it's your moral obligation to build great products, why you should wait as long as possible to draw a picture or create a prototype of your idea to what the Moon Landing can teach us about building better teams and products.
zh: 这次对话中的内容对每个人都有所助益，从为什么你应该考虑让设计向工程汇报，为什么构建伟大的产品是你的道德义务，为什么你应该尽可能长时间地等待去画一张图或为你的想法创建原型，到登月可以教会我们关于构建更好的团队和产品的什么知识。

speaker: Unknown
en: I could listen to Bob all day.
zh: 我可以一整天都听 Bob 讲话。

speaker: Unknown
en: I learned a ton from this conversation, including a bunch of really unique insights that I've never heard before.
zh: 我从这次对话中学到了很多，包括一堆我以前从未听过的真正独特的见解。

speaker: Unknown
en: A big thank you to Annie Warner, Andrew Hogan, Irene A, and Joff Redfern for suggesting questions for this conversation.
zh: 非常感谢 Annie Warner、Andrew Hogan、Irene A 和 Joff Redfern 为这次对话建议问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you enjoy this podcast, don't forget to subscribe and follow it in your favorite podcasting app or YouTube.
zh: 如果你喜欢这个播客，别忘了在你最喜欢的播客应用或 YouTube 中订阅和关注它。

en: Check it out lennysnewsletter.com and click bundle.
zh: 请访问 lennysnewsletter.com 并点击 bundle 查看。

zh: 有了这个，我为您介绍 Bob Baxley。

zh: 整集节目由 Stripe 赞助。

zh: 我之所以在这个播客上邀请了来自 Stripe 的嘉宾比任何其他公司都多，是有原因的。

en: You probably know them for their payments platform, which powers my newsletter, and also companies like Nvidia and Salesforce and Zoom and DoorDash.
zh: 你可能因为他们的支付平台而知道他们，该平台为我的简报提供支持，也为像 Nvidia、Salesforce、Zoom 和 DoorDash 这样的公司提供支持。

zh: 你可能不知道的是，他们还有其他几个产品可以帮助加速您的收入，例如 Stripe Billing，它为您可能听说过的公司 OpenAI、Anthropic、Figma、Atlassian 以及超过 300,000 家其他公司提供计费支持。

en: Stripe Billing lets you bill and manage customers however you want from simple recurring billing to usage-based billing to sales negotiated contracts.
zh: Stripe Billing 允许您按您想要的方式向客户计费和管理，从简单的经常性计费到基于使用量的计费，再到销售协商的合同。

en: There's also Stripe's Optimized Checkout Suite which is a plug and play super optimized payments flow that natively supports over 100 global dynamic payment methods.
zh: 还有 Stripe 的优化结账套件，这是一个即插即用的超级优化支付流程，原生支持超过 100 种全球动态支付方式。

zh: 还有一个名为 LINQ 的产品，这是一个专门为提高您的结账转化率而构建的加速结账体验。

speaker: Unknown
en: Every single one of the Forbes top 50 AI companies that have a product in the market today use Stripe to monetize it.
zh: 如今所有拥有产品的 Forbes 前 50 名 AI 公司，每一家都使用 Stripe 将其变现。

zh: 财富 100 强公司中有一半使用 Stripe。

zh: 每年有 1.4 万亿美元流经 Stripe，这相当于全球 GDP 的 1% 以上。

zh: 使用 Stripe 来处理您所有与支付相关的需求、计费、管理收入运营，以及启动或发明新的商业模式。

speaker: Unknown
en: Bob, thank you so much for being here and welcome to the podcast.
zh: Bob，非常感谢你来到这里并欢迎来到播客。

speaker: Unknown
en: Lenny, thank you so much.
zh: Lenny，非常感谢你。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thanks for having me, but also just thank you for what you do.
zh: 谢谢你的邀请，也感谢你所做的一切。

speaker: Unknown
en: We are still in early days to try to figure out how to make software together.
zh: 我们仍处于早期阶段，试图弄清楚如何一起制作软件。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think of it like where the film industry was in the 1920s.
zh: 我把这想象为电影行业在 1920 年代所处的位置。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've had our talkie moment.
zh: 我们已经经历了我们的“有声电影”时刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're on the cusp of having our shift to color movement, but we're still trying to figure out how to make movies and a podcast like yours specifically yours I think is one of the greatest resources we have for learning from one another.
zh: 我们正处于向“彩色电影”转变的风口浪尖，但我们仍在试图弄清楚如何制作电影，而像你这样的播客——特别是你的——我认为是我们相互学习的最大资源之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: I appreciate all you're doing for the community and for helping us as a community make better software.
zh: 我很感激你为社区所做的一切，以及作为社区帮助我们制作更好的软件。

speaker: Unknown
en: Wow.
zh: 哇。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, I really appreciate that.
zh: 好的，我真的非常感激。

speaker: Unknown
en: That means a lot coming from you.
zh: 这话从你嘴里说出来分量很重。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's so much I want to talk about in our conversation.
zh: 在我们的对话中，我有太多话题想聊了。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a story that I hear that you often tell, which is when somebody asked Steve Jobs once, what is your favorite product that you've built that you work on?
zh: 我听到一个你经常讲的故事，就是有一次有人问 Steve Jobs，你制造或参与的最喜欢的产品是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: And his answer, what's that story?
zh: 他的回答是什么，那个故事是怎样的？

speaker: Unknown
en: So I actually can't remember where I heard this, but I believe the story's true.
zh: 所以我其实不记得我在哪儿听到的这个，但我相信这个故事是真的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Steve at one point was recounting the products that he had created that he was most proud of, and if I recall the whole list, it was the Apple II, the Mac, the iPod, the iPhone, I think Apple retail was in the list and then he said Apple itself.
zh: Steve 在某个时刻正在细数他创造的他最引以为豪的产品，如果我没记错整个清单，那是 Apple II、Mac、iPod、iPhone，我想 Apple 零售店也在清单里，然后他说了 Apple 本身。

speaker: Unknown
en: When I heard that and when I've reflected on it, that is the longest lasting thing.
zh: 当我听到那个并且当我反思它时，那是持续时间最久的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: I remember there was also a story that Steve was talking to, I think it was either Ed Catmull or John Lasseter at Pixar, and he said, "Everything we make is going to be a doorstop in three years, but the stuff you guys make, they're still going to be watching in 100 years."
zh: 我记得也有一个故事是 Steve 在跟，我想是 Pixar 的 Ed Catmull 或者 John Lasseter 说话，他说，“我们要制造的每样东西在三年后都会变成镇纸，但你们家伙制造的东西，他们在 100 年后还会看。”

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think Steve had some concept of the longevity of these things.
zh: 所以我认为 Steve 对这些东西的长寿性有一些概念。

speaker: Unknown
en: They knew the products themselves were very ephemeral, but there's something about the culture of Apple that's lasted a very long time and I personally believe will last for some time yet to come.
zh: 他们知道产品本身是非常短暂的，但关于 Apple 的文化有一些东西持续了很长时间，我个人认为它还会持续一段时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a way of making decisions, it's a way of behaving, it's a way of seeing the value of technology in the world and it infuses everything in that company.
zh: 它是一种做决策的方式，它是一种行为举止的方式，它是一种看待世界中的技术价值的方式，它渗透了那家公司的一切。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean everything from the checkout system when you go to the receptionist to what it's like in the cafeteria.
zh: 我是指一切，从你去接待员那里的结账系统到自助餐厅是什么样子的。

speaker: Unknown
en: At least when I was there, they had patented the pizza box because they had reinvented the pizza box that you would get at Cafe Max because the whole company is constantly asking how can the thing that I'm working on be a little bit better?
zh: 至少当我在那里的时候，他们给披萨盒申请了专利，因为他们重新发明了你在 Cafe Max 拿到的披萨盒，因为整个公司都在不断询问，我正在做的东西怎么能变得更好一点？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that was something Steve brought to them and had them constantly asking that question.
zh: 我认为那是 Steve 给他们带来的东西，并且让他们不断询问那个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: One more Apple question then I'll move on to other stuff.
zh: 再问一个关于 Apple 的问题，然后我会转移到其他事情上。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why do you think that people that have left Apple, a lot of amazing things haven't emerged from people that have left?
zh: 为什么你认为那些离开了 Apple 的人，很多令人惊叹的事情并没有从那些离开的人中涌现出来？

speaker: Unknown
en: Humane was a recent example.
zh: Humane 是最近的一个例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're recording this the day after Jony Ive Open AI emerged so we'll see what happens there but just feels like there hasn't been a ton of alumni that have built incredible things.
zh: 我们录制这个是在 Jony Ive Open AI 出现后的第二天，所以我们会看看那里会发生什么，但感觉并没有很多校友建立了令人难以置信的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Obviously Tony Fadell would be one with Nest and he'd be an outlier.
zh: 显然 Tony Fadell 会是其中之一，带着 Nest，他会是一个异类。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the people that... I went to Pinterest and did not have a successful time in my year and a half at Pinterest.
zh: 我认为那些人……我去了 Pinterest 并且在我在 Pinterest 的一年半里没有成功的时光。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think my own particular mistake, and I've seen this with some other Apple executives as well as we went directly from Apple, I left Apple on a Friday and I started Pinterest on a Monday.
zh: 我认为我自己的特殊错误，而且我看到其他一些 Apple 高管也是如此，因为我们直接从 Apple 过渡，我在一个星期五离开了 Apple 并且我在一个星期一开始了 Pinterest。

speaker: Unknown
en: I didn't give myself time to recalibrate to the Pinterest culture.
zh: 我没有给自己时间重新校准到 Pinterest 的文化。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think at some level, a lot of the challenge is that Apple, and it's not just Apple, I think every major tech company, they have really powerful cultures.
zh: 我认为在某种程度上，很多挑战在于 Apple，而且不只是 Apple，我认为每个主要的科技公司，它们都有非常强大的文化。

speaker: Unknown
en: You get indoctrinated into all those standards and it's really deep.
zh: 你被灌输了所有那些标准，而且它真的非常深。

speaker: Unknown
en: It fuses all of your behavior and how you conduct yourself in the company, away from the company.
zh: 它融合了你所有的行为以及你在公司内外如何表现自己。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's pretty hard to immigrate successfully from one of those environments to another.
zh: 我认为要成功地从一个环境迁移到另一个环境是非常难的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Apple is one of the strongest cultures and there's not many other cultures that natively operate like that.
zh: Apple 是最强大的文化之一，没有多少其他文化原生像那样运作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Airbnb is one exception.
zh: Airbnb 是一个例外。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you have guys like Hiroki Asai who leads all of marketing and all of product and Hiroki is crushing at Airbnb.
zh: 所以你有像 Hiroki Asai 这样的人，他领导所有的营销和所有的产品，而且 Hiroki 在 Airbnb 表现得非常出色。

speaker: Unknown
en: He was incredibly successful at Apple.
zh: 他在 Apple 非常成功。

speaker: Unknown
en: It also should be noted that he had, it was a multi-year gap between the time he left Apple and the time he started Airbnb.
zh: 还应该注意的是，他有一个多年的空档期，在他离开 Apple 的时间和他开始 Airbnb 的时间之间。

speaker: Unknown
en: He gave himself a little bit of time to get through the... At Apple, I think it was Tim or Steve used to talk about the Apple car wash.
zh: 他给自己了一点时间来度过……在 Apple，我想是 Tim 或者 Steve 过去常谈论 Apple 洗车。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then when you started Apple, they kind of had to take you through the car wash and get off all that stuff that you'd accumulated at other places.
zh: 然后当你开始 Apple 时，他们有点不得不带你去过洗车，洗掉所有你在其他地方积累的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: It turns out there's a car wash you need to go through when you leave Apple as well.
zh: 事实证明，当你离开 Apple 时也需要过一个洗车。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think Hiroki gave himself time to do that and I think that's probably a lot of why he's been so successful at Airbnb.
zh: 所以我认为 Hiroki 给自己时间去做那件事，我认为这可能就是为什么他在 Airbnb 如此成功的很大一部分原因。

speaker: Unknown
en: The thing I took away from Apple, and I think this is true for anybody changing from one major culture to another is most likely the new place hires you because of the values of the organization you left, but not the behaviors.
zh: 我从 Apple 带走的东西，我认为这对任何从一个主要文化转换到另一个文化的人来说都是真的，很可能是新地方雇佣你是因你离开的组织的价值观，而不是行为。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think it's important to recalibrate and say, well, I want to hold onto these values.
zh: 所以我认为重新校准并说，好吧，我想坚持这些价值观，这很重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: So at Apple, attention to detail, product excellence, doing everything you can for the customer and the user so try to hold onto those values but then think, okay, how are those values best expressed in this culture?
zh: 所以在 Apple，关注细节、产品卓越、为客户和用户做你所能做的一切，所以尝试坚持这些价值观，但是要想，好吧，这些价值观在这种文化中如何最好地表达？

speaker: Unknown
en: I was more successful at expressing those values in the culture of ThoughtSpot, which was my last job than I was in the culture of Pinterest.
zh: 我在 ThoughtSpot 的文化中更成功地表达了那些价值观，那是我最后一份工作，比我在 Pinterest 的文化中更成功。

speaker: Unknown
en: If I had to do it again, I could probably do better at Pinterest.
zh: 如果我必须再做一次，我也许可以在 Pinterest 做得更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that's useful for anybody leaving one very specific culture and going someplace else, try to hold onto the values but not the behaviors.
zh: 我认为这对任何离开一个非常特定的文化并去往别处的人来说都是有用的，尝试坚持价值观而不是行为。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is so interesting and I appreciate you sharing that, the way you described it that it wasn't a successful stint at Pinterest.
zh: 这太有趣了，我很感激你分享那个，你描述它的那种方式，你在 Pinterest 的一段时光并不成功。

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of people don't share that sort of story and don't put it that way.
zh: 很多人不分享那种故事，也不会那样表述。

speaker: Unknown
en: They see on their LinkedIn, oh, a head of design at Pinterest.
zh: 他们在他们的 LinkedIn 上看到，哦，Pinterest 的设计主管。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, amazing so cool.
zh: 哦，太棒了，真酷。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then if you're like, oh, okay, but it didn't work out that well, I think that's really interesting.
zh: 然后如果你像，哦，好吧，但结果不太好，我认为这真的很有趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is there anything more you can share there about what you learned for other people to maybe avoid that sort of situation?
zh: 那里还有什么你能多分享一点关于你学到了什么以便其他人也许能避免那种情况吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Anything you took away from that experience?
zh: 你从那次经历中带走了什么吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: One of my friends that was at Pinterest, I'm still friends with, he said, "I just thought of it as you bounced off the culture."
zh: 我的一个在 Pinterest 的朋友，我还是朋友，他说，“我就把它看作你从文化上反弹了。”

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that's kind of the way to think of it.
zh: 我认为那是思考这个问题的一种方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: I came in thinking I was supposed to behave the way I behaved at Apple, which is very direct, fighting hard.
zh: 我进来时以为我应该按照我在苹果时的行为方式行事，那就是非常直接，努力争取。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everybody cares about each other.
zh: 每个人都互相关心。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's never insulting, but it's intense.
zh: 从不带有侮辱性，但很激烈。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's not really where Pinterest was at the time.
zh: 这真的不是当时 Pinterest 所处的状态。

speaker: Unknown
en: Again, all this is a decade ago, so I don't know what any of these companies are like today, but at least when I was there, Pinterest had posters in every conference room that said, big poster that said, say the hard thing.
zh: 再次强调，这一切都是十年前的事了，所以我不知道这些公司今天是什么样，但至少当我在那里时，Pinterest 在每个会议室都有海报，上面写着，大海报写着，说难说的话。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, that's where Pinterest was at the time, and I can assure you nobody at Apple was having to remind you to say the hard thing.
zh: 嗯，那就是当时 Pinterest 的状态，我可以向你保证，在苹果没人需要提醒你来说难说的话。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I probably could have picked up on that better than I did.
zh: 所以我本可能比我实际做得更好地察觉到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'll say these careers are really hard and the higher up you go, people think of it like you're climbing a pyramid.
zh: 我会说这些职业生涯真的很难，而且你走得越高，人们把它想象成你在攀登金字塔。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think of it more like you're going out on a branch on a tree and the branch gets a lot more flimsy and can break and you can fall and you get buffeted about by the wind.
zh: 我更把它想象成你在走上树枝，树枝变得更脆弱，可能会折断，你可能会掉下来，你会被风吹得东倒西歪。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's often at a time in your life when there's a lot going on with your family, there could be things going on with your parents' health.
zh: 这通常发生在你生活中的这样一个时刻，你的家庭发生了很多事，你父母的健康可能出现问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: I lost my mother when I was at Pinterest.
zh: 我在 Pinterest 时失去了我的母亲。

speaker: Unknown
en: My kids were starting high school, so we're struggling with the teenage years.
zh: 我的孩子刚开始上高中，所以我们正在为青少年时期而挣扎。

speaker: Unknown
en: I had a long commute.
zh: 我通勤时间很长。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a lot going on and these jobs are super demanding.
zh: 发生了很多事，这些工作要求极高。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everything around you is changing really rapidly and you're under tremendous pressure because the financial and success stakes are super high.
zh: 你周围的一切都在非常迅速地变化，你承受着巨大的压力，因为财务和成功的风险超级高。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the people falling off of these jobs is the common use case.
zh: 我认为人们从这些工作上跌落是常见的情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is the common story.
zh: 那是常见的故事。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have a bias towards survivors and we all talk about how it looks like they made it to the top, but everybody that makes it to the top, there's hundreds of people that don't.
zh: 我们对幸存者有偏见，我们都谈论他们看起来是如何到达顶峰的，但对于每一个到达顶峰的人，都有数以百计的人没有。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of the things I took away when I was at Pinterest was I came to think that the job of a startup was to grow the founder so they could continue to lead the startup.
zh: 我在 Pinterest 时带走的一件事是，我开始认为初创公司的工作是培养创始人，以便他们能够继续领导初创公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think what's true for founders, also true for a lot of the other folks in the executive staff, it's very hard to grow emotionally and developmentally at the rate that the company grows.
zh: 我认为对创始人来说是真实的情况，对于高管团队中的许多其他人来说也是如此，在公司增长的速度下，在情感和发展上成长是非常困难的。

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of times I think people get outgrown by the role, and I saw that across Apple.
zh: 我认为很多时候人们跟不上角色的成长，我在 Apple 看到了这种情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've experienced that myself at different times in my career.
zh: 我在我的职业生涯不同时期亲身经历过这种情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: I see that happening with my friends and it feels like a failure.
zh: 我看到我的朋友身上发生这种情况，感觉像是一种失败。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, that is the human experience, that's what happens.
zh: 我的意思是，那是人类的经验，那就是发生的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's very hard to grow as fast as some of these companies are growing and we could debate the merits of Mark Zuckerberg for example.
zh: 很难像这些公司中的一些那样快速成长，我们可以辩论马克·扎克伯格的优缺点。

speaker: Unknown
en: But when you think about the trajectory from being a kid in a dorm room to within five years, Facebook's a big thing.
zh: 但是当你想想从宿舍里的一个孩子到五年内，Facebook 成为一个大事物的轨迹。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, think of your own life.
zh: 我的意思是，想想你自己的生活。

speaker: Unknown
en: Can you process that level of evolution and change?
zh: 你能处理那种程度的进化和变化吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know, I think that's really super hard to do that and stay balanced.
zh: 我不知道，我认为真的非常难做到这一点并保持平衡。

speaker: Unknown
en: And also keep doing that for so long.
zh: 而且还要坚持做这么久。

speaker: Unknown
en: There'll be founders, I think it was Brian's maybe first job or second job, and he's doing that now for 15 years in a row.
zh: 会有一些创始人，我想这可能是 Brian 的第一份或第二份工作，而他现在已经连续做了 15 年了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, founders, it's their life.
zh: 噢，创始人，那是他们的生活。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's very unusual to see founders move out.
zh: 看到创始人离开是非常罕见的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I had this other theory that a startup is still a startup until the founder moves aside.
zh: 我有另一个理论，即初创公司仍然是初创公司，直到创始人离开。

speaker: Unknown
en: By my definition of even Meta is still a startup in a way that Amazon's not, and Airbnb is still a startup in a way that Pinterest is not because Ben's moved on.
zh: 根据我对初创公司的定义，甚至连 Meta 在某种意义上仍然是初创公司，而 Amazon 不是，Airbnb 在某种意义上仍然是初创公司，而 Pinterest 不是，因为 Ben 已经离开了。

speaker: Unknown
en: You don't find out if the culture can sustain itself until the founders are gone and then you really see what's going to happen.
zh: 在创始人离开之前，你不会发现文化是否能够自我维持，然后你才能真正看到将会发生什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just to close the loop here, one takeaway here that I think is really interesting is that you can fail in a job and things will be okay.
zh: 为了在这里做个了结，我认为一个非常有趣的收获是，你可以在工作中失败，而一切都会好起来的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Clearly you're doing A okay and having a place that doesn't work out, doesn't destroy your career, which I think a lot of people feel like if they're not doing well in their current job, it's over.
zh: 显然你现在做得很好，在一个不合适的地方并不意味着会毁掉你的职业生涯，我认为很多人觉得如果他们在目前的工作中做得不好，那就完了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Things are all going to go downhill
zh: 一切都会走下坡路

speaker: Unknown
en: Your career's not your life.
zh: 你的职业生涯不是你的生活。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a lot more to it than that.
zh: 它比那要多得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then just to give someone something tactical here, so you've realized the culture of Pinterest, you bounced off of it.
zh: 然后只是在这里给某人一些战术性的建议，所以你已经意识到了 Pinterest 的文化，你反弹了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I love that metaphor.
zh: 我喜欢那个隐喻。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you were to, when you're looking at new companies, what's one thing you look at or a question you ask or something you now look at to make sure you avoid that in the future, that culture clash?
zh: 如果你要，当你寻找新公司时，你关注的一件事或者你问的一个问题，或者你现在关注的某件事，是为了确保你在未来避免那种文化冲突？

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm fortunate at this stage of my career that I usually get to interview with the CEO or the founders or something like that.
zh: 我在这个职业生涯阶段很幸运，我通常可以与 CEO 或创始人或类似的人面试。

speaker: Unknown
en: What I'm usually looking for is do they have a story as to why they believe in design?
zh: 我通常寻找的是他们是否有关于为什么相信设计的故事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Really in their heart and soul, do they care about design?
zh: 真的在他们的灵魂深处，他们在乎设计吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because if I go into a company that doesn't really value the thing that I do, I'm just not going to have a great time and I'm going to be constantly buffeting up against all sorts of people.
zh: 因为如果我进入一家不真正重视我所做的事情的公司，我就不会过得很好，而且我会不断地与各种人发生冲突。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to make sure I've got air cover from the highest people in the company setting the culture.
zh: 我想确保我有来自公司最高层人员的掩护，他们正在设定文化。

speaker: Unknown
en: In the case of, again, my most recent job was with a company called ThoughtSpot.
zh: 就像，再一次，我最近的工作是在一家叫 ThoughtSpot 的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: And ThoughtSpot was founded by a gentleman named Ajeet Singh, and Ajeet grew up in rural India, but he tells this really great story about he studied chemical engineering, he moves to the United States.
zh: ThoughtSpot 是由一位名叫 Ajeet Singh 的绅士创立的，Ajeet 在印度农村长大，但他讲了一个非常棒的故事，关于他学习化学工程，然后搬到了美国。

speaker: Unknown
en: Early in his career, he's working for Honeywell and they did a couple of engagements with IDEO.
zh: 在他职业生涯早期，他在霍尼韦尔工作，他们与 IDEO 有过几次合作。

speaker: Unknown
en: As a very young person, he got to see what IDEO did and he realized the power of design and he's taken that to all of his companies.
zh: 作为一个非常年轻的人，他有机会看到 IDEO 在做什么，他意识到了设计的力量，他把这一点带到了他所有的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: He started Nutanix before he came to ThoughtSpot, before he started ThoughtSpot.
zh: 他在来 ThoughtSpot 之前，在创立 ThoughtSpot 之前，创立了 Nutanix。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so when I heard that, I'm like, oh, this is a guy that gets design right from the very beginning.
zh: 所以当我听到这些时，我想，哦，这是一个从一开始就懂得设计的家伙。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've also come to believe that I actually have never seen a company that grafted design on after the founding.
zh: 我也开始相信，我从未见过一家公司在创立后将设计嫁接上去。

speaker: Unknown
en: I could name lots of companies that I think are kind of design led, not always designer led, but design led or design centric.
zh: 我可以列举很多我认为是以设计为主导的公司，并不总是由设计师主导，而是设计主导或以设计为中心。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I've never seen somebody grafted on after the fact.
zh: 但我从未见过有人在事后嫁接上去的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's there at the beginning in the root DNA or doesn't exist.
zh: 它要么在开始时就存在于根 DNA 中，要么就不存在。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the thing that I'm looking for when I interview is, is it there at the beginning?
zh: 所以我在面试时寻找的是，它一开始就在那里吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Can I get a credible story that tracks it back to that?
zh: 我能得到一个可信的故事，将其追溯到那个起点吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And if that's the case, then I think I can find a way to navigate in that culture.
zh: 如果是那样，那么我想我能找到一种方法在这种文化中航行。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have a shared value system in a way that as an American, I could immigrate to Australia and the culture would be slightly different, but we'd have a shared value system that I could relate to.
zh: 我们有一种共同的价值观体系，作为一个美国人，我可以移民到澳大利亚，文化会略有不同，但我们将有一种我可以关联的共同价值观体系。

speaker: Unknown
en: If I moved to, I don't know, Burma or China or something, it would be wildly more challenging because the base view of the world, the base understanding of the world's just different and it'd be much harder for me to adapt to that.
zh: 如果我搬到，我不知道，缅甸或中国或什么地方，那将会非常具有挑战性，因为对世界的基本看法，对世界的基本理解是不同的，对我来说适应起来要困难得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think a way to extrapolate that insight is just whatever function you're in, get a sense of how important that function is to that business.
zh: 我认为外推这种洞察力的一种方法是，无论你在哪个职能部门，都要了解该职能对该业务有多重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do the founders value engineering?
zh: 创始人重视工程吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Do they value product?
zh: 他们重视产品吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Do they value design?
zh: 他们重视设计吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Depending on who you are.
zh: 取决于你是谁。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why would you want to work in a place that doesn't value the thing that you do?
zh: 你为什么要在一个不重视你所做事情的地方工作？

speaker: Unknown
en: God, that would suck.
zh: 天啊，那太糟了。

speaker: Unknown
en: You actually have a really unique perspective on just what is design that I haven't heard before.
zh: 你实际上对设计究竟是什么有着非常独特的视角，这是我以前没有听过的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let me ask you that question is what is design?
zh: 让我问你这个问题，什么是设计？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, I'm going to go back to the Edward Tufte quote that I use all the time, which is design is clear thinking made visible.
zh: 好吧，我要回到我经常使用的 Edward Tufte 的名言，即设计是可见的清晰思考。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think most people when they talk about design, they think of it as the visual expression of an idea.
zh: 所以我认为大多数人谈论设计时，他们认为这是一种想法的视觉表达。

speaker: Unknown
en: They think of it as a team or a function or a group.
zh: 他们认为它是一个团队或一个职能或一个小组。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think of it as a holistic mindset.
zh: 我将其视为一种整体心态。

speaker: Unknown
en: When design thinking became big, I was always really confused because I didn't know how else you could think.
zh: 当设计思维变得流行时，我总是真的很困惑，因为我不知道你还能怎么思考。

speaker: Unknown
en: That was just how I naturally thought, which is design is trying to imagine the future you want to live in and then take the steps to make it real.
zh: 那只是我自然的思考方式，即设计是试图想象你想要生活的未来，然后采取步骤使其成为现实。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's living with a certain type of intentionality in almost a Buddhist type way, which is different from science, which is observational trying to understand.
zh: 它是以一种几乎佛教式的方式带着某种意图性生活，这不同于科学，科学是观察性的试图理解。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a little bit different from engineering, which is we kind of know where we want go at the end, but we're trying to go one step at a time versus design's trying to see some further out future state and account for a larger or a different set of constraints and issues than engineering or some of the other problem solving methodologies.
zh: 它与工程学略有不同，工程学是我们大概知道最后要去哪里，但我们试图一次走一步，而设计是试图看到更远的未来状态，并考虑比工程学或其他一些解决问题方法论更大或不同的一组约束和问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Again, I look at it as a company, does the company think in a design mindset and Apple does, Airbnb does.
zh: 同样，我把它看作一家公司，该公司是否以设计心态思考，苹果公司是的，Airbnb 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't get the sense that Google does and I don't get the sense that Amazon does.
zh: 我感觉谷歌不是，我感觉亚马逊不是。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's not a critique on them.
zh: 这不是对他们的批评。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think that those organizations are competing on design in the same way.
zh: 我认为这些组织并没有以同样的方式在设计上竞争。

speaker: Unknown
en: But again, I want to go work at a place that as an organization thinks in a design type method.
zh: 但同样，我想去一个作为一个组织以设计类型方法思考的地方工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Along those lines, a lot of people imagine every founder, every product builder is just, yes, I'd love amazing design.
zh: 沿着这些思路，很多人想象每个创始人，每个产品构建者只是，是的，我想要令人惊叹的设计。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'd love our products to be incredibly beautiful, intuitive, so easy for everyone to use and understand, but they don't actually invest in these areas and they don't put a lot of resources into the designing process.
zh: 我希望我们的产品非常漂亮、直观，让每个人都容易使用和理解，但他们实际上不在这些领域投资，他们也没有在设计过程中投入大量资源。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's the best pitch you can make and that you do make to companies to help them see the strategic value of design and the bottom of the value of design.
zh: 你能向公司提出的最好推销是什么，以及你确实向公司提出的推销，以帮助他们看到设计的战略价值和设计的底线价值。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let me back up and just dissect a little bit the way you described design, you described it in really tactical terms.
zh: 让我倒回来，只是稍微剖析一下你描述设计的方式，你用非常战术性的术语描述了它。

speaker: Unknown
en: You said beautiful, intuitive products that make sense.
zh: 你说漂亮、直观的产品，说得通。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it was something like that.
zh: 我想大概是那样。

speaker: Unknown
en: What you were describing was you were describing the part of the iceberg that sits above the water line, which is the result.
zh: 你描述的是你描述了冰山位于水线以上的部分，那是结果。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's one of the outcomes of design, but that's not the real heavy lifting of design.
zh: 这是设计的结果之一，但这不是设计的真正繁重工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Design is more like liberal arts or philosophy or something.
zh: 设计更像文科或哲学之类的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like what do we try to achieve at a much lower level?
zh: 这就像我们在更低的层面上试图实现什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: And so what I talk to founders and people about the value of design, what I'm pushing them on is when we can get organizational alignment around what we want to do philosophically, why do we exist?
zh: 所以当我与创始人和人们谈论设计的价值时，我推动他们的是当我们能在哲学层面上围绕我们想做的事情达成组织一致时，我们为什么存在？

speaker: Unknown
en: What's the vision for the company?
zh: 公司的愿景是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: How do all these things ladder up through vision, through mission, through specific tenets, design strategies.
zh: 所有这些东西如何通过愿景、通过使命、通过特定原则、设计策略向上攀登。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then into actual execution.
zh: 然后进入实际执行。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do we ladder that whole thing up so it makes sense as a whole?
zh: 我们要如何把整件事层层递进，使其在整体上变得合理？

speaker: Unknown
en: That's the magic of design.
zh: 这就是设计的魔力。

speaker: Unknown
en: The difference is when you design things, you end up with a bunch of bricks that are piled into a beautiful impenetrable wall.
zh: 区别在于，当你设计东西时，你会得到一堆砖块，它们被堆成了一堵美丽而无法逾越的墙。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you don't do that, you end up with a bunch of bricks scattered across the backyard and they don't really add up to anything.
zh: 如果你不那样做，你最终会得到一堆散落在后院的砖块，它们真的无法组成任何东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that's one of the things, if you look, again to go back to Apple, but we could also talk about Lego Lyca, Porsche, Airbnb, Patagonia, there's other companies that make sense as a design centered organization.
zh: 我认为这是其中一件事，如果你再看看 Apple，但我们也可以谈谈 Lego Lyca、Porsche、Airbnb、Patagonia，还有其他作为以设计为中心的组织而讲得通的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you think about everything they do, it all ladders together into one cohesive sensical thing.
zh: 如果你想想他们做的所有事情，它们都层层递进地结合成一个连贯的、合理的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's integrated.
zh: 它是集成的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Makes sense as a unit.
zh: 作为一个整体是合理的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that's a huge difference and an incredible strategic advantage because the company can operate with much greater efficiency.
zh: 我认为这是一个巨大的差异，也是一个令人难以置信的战略优势，因为公司可以以更高的效率运作。

speaker: Unknown
en: They can onboard new people and get them in line.
zh: 他们可以让新员工入职并让他们步调一致。

speaker: Unknown
en: Even Apple, for example, the team that designed the online store, we had six designers for a store that ran in 30 some odd countries, 12 and a half thousand instances of the store doing billions of dollars of revenue.
zh: 举一个 Apple 的例子，负责设计在线商店的团队，我们只有六名设计师，而这家店在 30 多个国家运营，有 12500 个商店实例，创造数十亿美元的收入。

speaker: Unknown
en: We had six designers.
zh: 我们有六名设计师。

speaker: Unknown
en: Any other company would've had 60 or more.
zh: 任何其他公司都会有 60 名或更多。

speaker: Unknown
en: Apple's able to operate with much smaller staff because they have real clarity of vision of what they're doing.
zh: Apple 能够用更少的员工运营，因为他们对正在做的事情有非常清晰的愿景。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the benefit of operating with a smaller staff is not just that it saves money on payroll, it's that you have... The way the minds come together to create something that feels like a single whole is a much higher chance when you have fewer people involved.
zh: 用更少的员工运营的好处不仅仅是在工资单上省钱，而是你有……当涉及的人更少时，思维聚集在一起创造出某种感觉像一个单一整体的东西的可能性要大得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: I joke about The Beatles.
zh: 我经常开玩笑说披头士。

speaker: Unknown
en: You get The Beatles with four people, you don't get The Beatles with eight people and you certainly don't get it with 24 people.
zh: 你有四个人就能得到披头士，你不可能有八个人得到披头士，你肯定不可能有 24 个人得到它。

speaker: Unknown
en: The teams get too big and you can't get that what Brian Eno calls scenius.
zh: 团队变得太大了，你就无法得到 Brian Eno 称为 scenius 的那种东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Brian Eno has this great word that he uses, scenius is the genius that comes when you have a group together.
zh: Brian Eno 有一个他使用的很棒的词，scenius 是当你有一个群体时产生的天才。

speaker: Unknown
en: Scenius is the collective idea of genius and I think that's something that's really magical that I've experienced in my career, but usually in smaller groups.
zh: Scenius 是天才的集体概念，我认为这是我在职业生涯中经历过的真正神奇的事情，但通常是在小群体中。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's hard to do with a giant group.
zh: 对于庞大的群体来说很难做到。

speaker: Unknown
en: I love this metaphor of The Beatles as the way most people describe this is designed by committee never works.
zh: 我喜欢用披头士作比喻，因为大多数人描述这种情况的方式是委员会设计从未成功过。

speaker: Unknown
en: I love that the way you describe it is the Beatles is like the ideal size a small group versus a committee.
zh: 我喜欢你描述它的方式，披头士就像是一个小团体的理想规模，而不是委员会。

speaker: Unknown
en: I just always have to point out to people that there are 20 people that worked on the original Mac.
zh: 我总是不得不向人们指出，原来的 Mac 有 20 个人参与了工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean it's 20 of them, that's it, 20.
zh: 我的意思是那是 20 个人，就这样，20 个。

speaker: Unknown
en: Susan Kare was one of them, Andy Hertzfeld, you go through the list, 20 of them are on the patent.
zh: Susan Kare 是其中之一，Andy Hertzfeld，你查看名单，专利上有 20 个人。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's 24 that are on the iPhone patent.
zh: iPhone 专利上有 24 个人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now there's other people involved, but generally there's 24 people on the iPhone patent.
zh: 现在还有其他人参与，但通常 iPhone 专利上有 24 个人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that was the team.
zh: 那就是团队。

speaker: Unknown
en: That was Project Purple that was doing that stuff.
zh: 那就是做这些事情的 Project Purple。

speaker: Unknown
en: These are not massive massive groups doing these things.
zh: 这些做这些事情的不是庞大的群体。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you had put a massive group, I don't know man, maybe it'd end up with the Zune or something completely different.
zh: 如果你放一个庞大的群体，我不知道伙计，也许它最终会变成 Zune 或者完全不同的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Who knows?
zh: 谁知道呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: They probably did have a massive group on the Zune.
zh: 他们可能确实在 Zune 上有一个庞大的群体。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, so there's something, four is too few for what we're trying to achieve at scale.
zh: 是的，所以有一些东西，对于我们要大规模实现的目标来说，四个太少了。

speaker: Unknown
en: But even if you look at Pixar, any good movie on the scripting and story side, it's usually a fairly small team.
zh: 但即使你看 Pixar，任何在剧本和故事方面的好电影，通常都是一个相当小的团队。

speaker: Unknown
en: Even when you move into character development, stuff like that, it's fairly small and then it really scales when you move into production.
zh: 即使当你进入角色开发之类的事情时，它也相当小，然后当你进入制作时它真的会扩大规模。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just hard to figure out something new to do together when there's too many people involved.
zh: 当有太多人参与时，很难一起想出新的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that word new is really key here.
zh: 我认为这个“新”词在这里真的很关键。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think when people hear this advice, they're thinking at their existing company, should we just keep our company small?
zh: 我认为当人们听到这个建议时，他们是在想在他们现有的公司，我们应该保持公司小规模吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Should we not scale this thing that we have?
zh: 我们不应该扩展我们拥有的这个东西吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think what you're describing, which I completely agree with is new stuff for sure you want to keep the team small and tight, but as things grow and scale, what's your take on just, okay, actually it's okay to have a lot of people on this.
zh: 我认为你描述的情况，我完全同意，对于新东西肯定要保持团队小而精，但随着事情的发展和扩大，你对好的，实际上在这里有很多人是可以的有什么看法？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, you have to bring a lot of people in once you figure out what you're doing.
zh: 嗯，一旦你弄清楚你在做什么，你就必须带很多人进来。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so to your point, once you realize you're building Disneyland and you've got the whole thing set and people know what it's about, then they can come in and understand, oh, I'm playing my piece over here.
zh: 因此针对你的观点，一旦你意识到你正在建造 Disneyland 并且你把整个东西都设定好了，人们知道它是关于什么的，然后他们就可以进来并理解，哦，我在这里扮演我的角色。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm supposed to design the line experience for the new ride sitting in Tomorrowland, but I know where that fits into this larger thing.
zh: 我应该为坐落在 Tomorrowland 的新游乐设施设计排队体验，但我知道它在这个更大的事情中处于什么位置。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think you can scale once you have clarity of vision, but it's very difficult to get vision with a lot of people.
zh: 我认为一旦你有清晰的愿景就可以扩展，但是有很多人很难获得愿景。

speaker: Unknown
en: Great.
zh: 很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that's really powerful advice.
zh: 我认为这是非常有力的建议。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just when you're starting something new.
zh: 就是当你开始新事情的时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: I actually had a CPA of N26 who was basically leading Google Hangouts, the initial launch of Google Hangouts, and he told the story of they put so many resources on it.
zh: 我实际上有一个 N26 的 CPA，他基本上领导了 Google Hangouts，Google Hangouts 的初次发布，他讲了一个故事，他们为此投入了如此多的资源。

speaker: Unknown
en: We got to win.
zh: 我们必须赢。

speaker: Unknown
en: We got to do this.
zh: 我们必须做到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Larry Page or Sergey was sitting next to him just like we got to make this work and putting everything they could into it and it didn't work out.
zh: Larry Page 或 Sergey 坐在他旁边，就像我们必须让这成功一样，把一切都投入进去，但结果没有成功。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that's-
zh: 而且我认为这-

speaker: Unknown
en: No, no, the more people you put in it, the slower everything becomes.
zh: 不，不，你投入的人越多，一切变得越慢。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to go back to something you said about what design is.
zh: 我想回到你刚才说的关于设计是什么的问题上。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think this is really interesting.
zh: 我觉得这非常有趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the way you described design to a lot of people, it sounds like that's like product management also and product leadership, setting, strategy, vision, figuring out how everything fits together.
zh: 你向很多人描述设计的方式听起来这也像产品管理和产品领导，设定、策略、愿景，搞清楚所有东西如何组合在一起。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think your experience here, I think Apple is a very different kind of company where design actually leads a lot of this.
zh: 我认为你在这方面的经验，我认为 Apple 是一种非常不同的公司，设计实际上主导了其中很多工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: At a lot of other companies, it doesn't work that way.
zh: 在很多其他公司，事情并非那样运作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Any thoughts?
zh: 有什么想法吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And just how you advise companies, think about the split between design and product management that aren't Apple.
zh: 以及你如何建议公司，思考设计团队与产品管理团队之间的分工，对于非 Apple 公司而言。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of the best lines I ever heard was from my friend Joseph O'Sullivan at dinner one night.
zh: 我听过的最好的话之一，是我朋友 Joseph O'Sullivan 一天晚上在晚餐时说的。

speaker: Unknown
en: He said saying a company is design led does not mean it's designer led.
zh: 他说说一家公司是由设计主导的并不意味着它是由设计师主导的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so what I try to hammer home with people is that when I talk about design as a mindset, I'm talking about it as a mindset.
zh: 所以我试图向人们强调的是，当我把设计作为一种思维模式谈论时，我是把它作为一种思维模式来谈论。

speaker: Unknown
en: Anybody could have that mindset functioning in any role, any designer could have a product mindset.
zh: 任何人在任何角色中都可以拥有那种思维模式，任何设计师都可以拥有产品思维模式。

speaker: Unknown
en: In fact, I think that's a lot of what the design community is trying to get at now when they say designers should be speaking the language of business.
zh: 事实上，我认为这也是现在设计界试图达到的目标，当他们说设计师应该说商业的语言时。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think what they're saying is designers need to inhabit the product mindset as well.
zh: 我认为他们说的是设计师也需要占据产品思维模式。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe to some degree even the sales mindset.
zh: 也许在某种程度上甚至是销售思维模式。

speaker: Unknown
en: Look, both functions matter.
zh: 看，这两个职能都很重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: I look at my counterparts in product and I assume that they're much better connected to the customer, that they understand much better the business realities, and I expect them to drive the roadmap.
zh: 我看我在产品方面的对应方，我假设他们与客户连接得更好，他们更了解商业现实，我期望他们来驱动路线图。

speaker: Unknown
en: I may have some points of view on the roadmap.
zh: 我可能对路线图有一些看法。

speaker: Unknown
en: I may offer some critique.
zh: 我可能会提供一些批评。

speaker: Unknown
en: I may have my own suggestions and agenda in there.
zh: 我可能在那里有我自己的建议和议程。

speaker: Unknown
en: But once they say this is the roadmap, I have to believe that they're right and I don't try to bleed into their space.
zh: 但一旦他们说了这是路线图，我就必须相信他们是对的，我不试图渗入到他们的空间。

speaker: Unknown
en: I very much believe that once you get into a company, your job is to figure out your role and respect the boundaries between the different groups.
zh: 我非常相信，一旦你进入一家公司，你的工作就是搞清楚你的角色并尊重不同群体之间的界限。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm like, you guys tell us what you need us to do, what the features need to be, when they need to be delivered, what the issues are, and then give us the time and space to come up with a solution to those problems.
zh: 我想说的是，你们告诉我们需要做什么，功能需要是什么，何时交付，问题是什么，然后给我们时间和空间去想出解决这些问题的方案。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we can work together to decide whether or not our solutions actually solve the problem as you understand it, but I'll stay out of your roadmap and you stay out of my design stop and let's try to get to the promised land together.
zh: 然后我们可以一起决定我们的解决方案是否真的解决了你所理解的问题，但我会远离你的路线图，你远离我的设计，让我们试着一起到达应许之地。

speaker: Unknown
en: I assume that the product managers, particularly in enterprise SaaS companies, like my team, ThoughtSpot did data analytics.
zh: 我假设产品经理，特别是在企业 SaaS 公司，比如我在 ThoughtSpot 的团队做数据分析。

speaker: Unknown
en: My team didn't know anything about data analytics.
zh: 我的团队对数据分析一无所知。

speaker: Unknown
en: We didn't have any of that insight.
zh: 我们没有任何那种洞察力。

speaker: Unknown
en: We didn't have the bandwidth, the mental horsepower to go out and do that stuff.
zh: 我们没有带宽，没有脑力出去做那些事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: We had our hands full just trying to figure out the UI.
zh: 我们的手已经满了，光是试图搞清楚 UI。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's one of the points I try to make too, when people are starting to theorize that gen AI can remove teammates and oh, the designers don't need engineers and the PMs don't need the designers and everybody thinks they can throw engineering overboard.
zh: 这也是我试图提出的观点之一，当人们开始理论化生成式 AI 可以移除队友，哦，设计师不需要工程师，PM 不需要设计师，每个人都认为他们可以把工程师扔到船外。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm like, stop it.
zh: 我就说，停。

speaker: Unknown
en: We all need each other and we need each other because we need those different mindsets.
zh: 我们彼此需要，我们需要彼此是因为我们需要那些不同的思维模式。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of those mindsets inhabits somebody's head completely.
zh: 其中一种思维模式完全占据某人的头脑。

speaker: Unknown
en: I just don't think you can simultaneously hold multiple mindsets in your head.
zh: 我只是不认为你可以同时在头脑中保持多种思维模式。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not that one of my PM counterparts couldn't bring a lot to the design table, it's just I need you to play that position.
zh: 不是我的 PM 对应方不能给设计桌带来很多贡献，只是我需要你去打那个位置。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like in baseball, the second-
zh: 就像在棒球里，二垒手-

speaker: Unknown
en: Like in baseball, the second baseman doesn't cover first.
zh: 就像在棒球里，二垒手不守一垒。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's not how it works.
zh: 那不是它运作的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everybody's got to spread the field and play their position so we can take care of the whole thing and respect that together we're going to come up with something better than any one of us would've come up with alone and embrace the creative tension, welcome it.
zh: 每个人都必须分散到场地上并打自己的位置，这样我们可以照顾整个事情，并尊重在一起我们会拿出比我们任何一个人单独想出的更好的东西，并拥抱创造性的张力，欢迎它。

speaker: Unknown
en: We still have to all go out to lunch and love each other and have fun together and keep in mind that we're having fun together, but I like the rub.
zh: 我们仍然必须一起出去吃午饭，彼此相爱，一起玩得开心，并记住我们要在一起玩得开心，但我喜欢这种摩擦。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's where all the magic happens.
zh: 那就是所有魔法发生的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: That was a very illuminating clarification.
zh: 那是一个非常具有启发性的澄清。

speaker: Unknown
en: Something else that I heard you believe that I haven't heard before is that design share report to engineering.
zh: 我听你相信的另一样我以前没听过的事情是，设计团队应该向工程部门汇报。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I'll say that every company culture is different and different organizations work in different ways.
zh: 所以我会说每个公司的文化都是不同的，不同的组织以不同的方式工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: In my experience, I think that design is most successful at impacting what ships at the end if design is considered phase zero of the engineering process, rather than a by product or a part of the product process.
zh: 根据我的经验，我认为设计在最终影响交付的东西方面是最成功的，如果设计被认为是工程过程的第零阶段，而不是副产品或产品过程的一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: What I've seen happen over and over in my experience, a ThoughtSpot, Pinterest, other places when you're working directly with product, it's easy to leave engineering out of the loop and product and design can go cook up stuff that doesn't quite make sense technically or is really hard to implement or is just a bridge too far.
zh: 在我的经验中，在 ThoughtSpot、Pinterest 和其他地方一遍又一遍看到的是，当你直接与产品合作时，很容易把工程排除在循环之外，产品和设计可以去搞出一些技术上不太说得通的东西，或者真的很难实施，或者只是太远了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that engineering doesn't feel like they're a part of it, so you bring them at the end and they haven't really been brought along so they don't quite understand how to extrapolate from the specs you make into what should really ship.
zh: 我认为工程团队感觉他们不是其中的一部分，所以你在最后才带上他们，而他们并没有真正被带在身边，所以他们不太理解如何从你制定的需求规格说明（specs）推断出真正应该交付（ship）的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe they don't bring the same level of enthusiasm to it, because they haven't been brought along.
zh: 也许他们对此没有带来同样的热情，因为他们没有被一路带上。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think there's something about having the design and engineering team very tightly connected and kind of living together.
zh: 所以我认为有一点很重要，就是让设计和工程团队紧密联系并基本上生活在一起。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's not that you have to do that structurally from an organization point of view, but it's hard-pressed if you don't.
zh: 这并不是说从组织架构的角度来看你必须这样做，但如果你不这样做，就会感到很困难。

speaker: Unknown
en: I also think you can just account for timelines and costs and things better when design's part of engineering.
zh: 我还认为，当设计成为工程的一部分时，你可以更好地核算时间表、成本和其他事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And many of my design friends will push back on this and they'll say design should be its own thing and it should be an independent group and we should have three co-equal branches of government, and that's a solid argument as well, and there's some places where that works beautifully.
zh: 我的许多设计朋友会反驳这一点，他们会说设计应该是它自己的东西，应该是一个独立的组织，我们应该有三个平等的政府部门分支，这也是一个可靠的论点，而且在某些地方这运作得非常好。

speaker: Unknown
en: My experiences at design rarely has a budget or an army, and so it's very hard for them to really hold their own in that sort of a setting.
zh: 我的经验是，设计很少有预算或一支大军，所以在这种环境中，他们很难真正坚持自己的立场。

speaker: Unknown
en: Also, although you'll see people argue with me on LinkedIn about how design needs to be measured and we need to have metrics and be held accountable for a number, I don't really believe that in my heart.
zh: 此外，虽然你会看到人们在 LinkedIn 上与我争论，认为设计需要被衡量，我们需要有指标，并要对一个数字负责，但在我的内心深处并不真正相信这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've just never seen a number that you could apply to design that we could reliably affect.
zh: 我从未见过一个可以应用于设计的数字，而我们能够可靠地对其产生影响。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think it's very hard to hold design as an organization accountable for a particular outcome the way that most of the other C-level roles are held accountable.
zh: 所以我认为，很难像大多数其他 C-level 角色被问责那样，让设计作为一个组织对特定的结果负责。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sales has a number, engineering has very specific expectations, product has very specific expectations.
zh: 销售有一个数字，工程有非常具体的期望，产品有非常具体的期望。

speaker: Unknown
en: And although I know this will frustrate some of my friends, I just haven't been able to figure out how that works for design.
zh: 虽然我知道这会让我的一些朋友感到沮丧，但我一直没能弄清楚这对设计是如何运作的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And again, it can vary from culture to culture.
zh: 而且，这可能会因文化而异。

speaker: Unknown
en: Certainly there's very successful chief design officers and we could go through the list.
zh: 当然，也有非常成功的首席设计官（chief design officers），我们可以列举一下名单。

speaker: Unknown
en: I just think in many companies it's a stretch, it's just hard.
zh: 我只是认为在许多公司，这有点牵强，就是很难。

speaker: Unknown
en: What I see work, and I'm curious to get your take is just product, engineering, design have exactly the same goal and the more everyone... And their performance as an employee is tied to the same thing essentially because then everyone is pushing in the same direction versus like, oh, I have my engineering goal, I have my design goal, I have my PM goal, and just creates all kinds of weird incentives.
zh: 我看到行之有效的做法，我也很想知道你的看法，就是产品、工程、设计有完全相同的目标，而且每个人越……而且他们作为员工的绩效本质上与同一件事挂钩，因为这样每个人都在朝同一个方向努力，而不是像，噢，我有我的工程目标，我有我的设计目标，我有我的 PM（产品经理）目标，这只会产生各种奇怪的激励。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, look, I would kind of defer to you on that, honestly.
zh: 是的，看，说实话，在这方面我多少会听从你的意见。

speaker: Unknown
en: You've talked to a lot more people across a lot more companies, so you have a much broader set of information you're working with.
zh: 你与更多公司的人交谈过，所以你手头掌握的信息范围要广泛得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you add my whole career together, I've worked at maybe half a dozen places, so a fairly limited sample set.
zh: 如果你把我整个职业生涯加起来，我也许只在六七个地方工作过，所以样本集相当有限。

speaker: Unknown
en: And every design team that I've ever been a part of, I've been a part of.
zh: 而且我参与的每一个设计团队，我都曾是其中的一员。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I also kind of have a biased view as to what didn't work for me in those particular organizations.
zh: 所以对于这些特定组织中什么对我不起作用，我也持有某种带有偏见的看法。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'll go back to what I said, every company's different, every culture is slightly different.
zh: 我回到我刚才说的话，每家公司都不同，每种文化都略有不同。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not one size fits all.
zh: 这不是一刀切的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I point out the idea of design reporting to engineering just because I don't think people consider the possibility often enough.
zh: 我指出设计向工程汇报这一想法，只是因为我认为人们往往没有足够频繁地考虑这种可能性。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's three options, design is its own thing, design is part of product, design is part of engineering.
zh: 所以有三个选项，设计是独立的，设计是产品的一部分，设计是工程的一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think there's a moment when you can back up and make an intelligent choice about the pros and cons for each of those options inside your org.
zh: 我认为有那么一个时刻，你可以退一步，就这每个选项在你组织内部的优缺点做出明智的选择。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I would encourage people to just take a design mentality and put on that designer mindset just for a moment and say, well, what's the thing that we're trying to produce?
zh: 所以我鼓励人们只是采用一种设计心态，并暂时戴上设计师的思维帽，说好吧，我们试图生产的东西是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: What's the incentives that we're trying to create?
zh: 我们试图创造的激励是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: What's the future state that we're trying to get to?
zh: 我们试图到达的未来状态是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: And which of these three options, permutations is going to help us get there the best?
zh: 而这三个选项中的哪一个，排列组合将能帮助我们最好地到达那里？

speaker: Unknown
en: I love how radical this idea is.
zh: 我喜欢这个想法的激进程度。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've not heard it.
zh: 我没听说过这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think designers will be like, " You stop it.
zh: 我认为设计师们会说，“你住手。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just stop it."
zh: 住手就好。”

speaker: Unknown
en: So have you operated this way?
zh: 那你就是这样运作的吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Have you had design report to engineering in companies you've worked at?
zh: 你在你工作过的公司里有让设计向工程汇报吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Sorry, but that's how it worked at Apple the whole time under Steve.
zh: 抱歉，但这就是在 Steve（史蒂夫）领导下 Apple（苹果）一直以来的运作方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: Design always reported to engineering.
zh: 设计总是向工程汇报。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now I think it's structured a little bit differently, but design has always been part of engineering at Apple, so I saw it work quite effectively there obviously.
zh: 现在我认为它的结构略有不同，但在 Apple，设计一直是工程的一部分，所以我在那里看到它非常有效地运作，显然如此。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's so interesting.
zh: 真的很有趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, so say just to give someone something very tactical to do on their team, say they don't want to go to this extreme and move the design org under engineering, what's something you've seen work that helps achieve similar outcomes with having engineers integrated early in the design process?
zh: 好的，所以举个非常具体的例子，给他们团队里可以做的事情，假设他们不想走这么极端，把设计组织搬到工程下面，你看到有什么行之有效的方法可以帮助实现类似的结果，让工程师在设计过程的早期就参与进来？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, look, I think you have to find some way that you are able to identify a few people in engineering that I refer to as creative technologists.
zh: 是的，看，我认为你必须找到某种方法，能够识别出工程领域的一些我称之为创意技术人员（creative technologists）的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: So these are people that can come into what's ultimately kind of a fairly airy-fairy philosophical discussion about what we could do and what's right from a conceptual model perspective.
zh: 所以这些人可以进入最终那种相当空泛的哲学讨论，讨论我们可以做什么，以及从概念模型的角度来看什么是正确的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Ultimately, it's sort of a philosophy issue.
zh: 最终，这有点像是一个哲学问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's not that many PMs or engineers that can sit in that space and be comfortable with the ambiguity of it all.
zh: 并没有多少 PM 或工程师能够在这个空间里坐得住，并对所有这些模糊性感到自在。

speaker: Unknown
en: A PM's likely going to come in and they're going to say, okay, well that was a great one hour.
zh: PM 很可能会进来，然后说，好吧，那真是很棒的一小时。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's the next step?
zh: 下一步是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: And as a designer I'm always like, well, the next step is we're going to have another meeting and we're going to talk again.
zh: 而作为设计师，我总是觉得，好吧，下一步是我们再开个会，我们要再谈一次。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the engineers oftentimes when they're starting to hear different ideas, they're already cutting into the code and they're trying to figure out what's hard and what's easy.
zh: 而工程师们通常当他们开始听到不同的想法时，他们已经开始切入代码了，并且他们试图弄清楚什么是难的，什么是容易的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think the trick is at the beginning, can you find a small group of people from the different functions that can sit with the ambiguity of the space and talk through a broad range of ideas to identify the direction we want to go into?
zh: 所以我认为诀窍在于在开始的时候，你能不能从不同的职能部门找到一小群人，他们能够忍受这个空间的模糊性，并通过讨论广泛的想法来确定我们想要进入的方向？

speaker: Unknown
en: And then once everybody kind of falls in love with the direction, then you can go into the more tactical mindset of, okay, well, when we can ship it and who can we show it to and how are we going to code it and when's it going to go live and all those sorts of things.
zh: 然后一旦每个人都爱上了这个方向，你就可以进入更战术性的思维模式，好吧，我们要什么时候发布，我们可以展示给谁看，我们要怎么编码它，它什么时候上线，以及所有这类事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the trick is to try to find a group that can sit, again, in the ambiguous maybe space.
zh: 但诀窍在于试图找到一个能够再次处于模棱两可的“可能”空间中的群体。

speaker: Unknown
en: I do think it's critical to have everybody together at the beginning so they all feel like they're part of it.
zh: 我确实认为在开始时把每个人聚集在一起至关重要，这样他们都会觉得自己是其中的一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the worst thing is when you bring something fully baked... Well, the worst thing when you bring something fully baked to anybody for their approval.
zh: 最糟糕的是当你把一个完全成熟的东西拿给……好吧，当你把一个完全成熟的东西拿给任何人批准时，最糟糕的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: We could talk about this when you take a final design to an exec and an exec sees it for the first time in a high resolution state, I'll get to that in a second.
zh: 我们可以谈谈这一点，当你把最终设计拿给一位高管看，而这位高管第一次看到它的高分辨率状态时，我稍后会讲到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: But when you go to an engineering team says, "Hey, we've been working in the lab for six months and we have this thing that we love it and we just can't wait for you guys to build it, and here it is," I don't know, [inaudible 00:32:54] mention here.
zh: 但当你去一个工程团队那里说，“嘿，我们在实验室里已经工作了六个月，我们有一个我们很喜欢的东西，我们迫不及待想让你们来构建它，就是这个，”我不知道，[听不清 00:32:54] 这里提到。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're going to be excited about.
zh: 他们会对此感到兴奋。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're not order takers.
zh: 他们不是接单员。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you make them part of the process?
zh: 你如何让他们成为流程的一部分？

speaker: Unknown
en: And every product of consequence that I worked on, there was some moment when we were showing it to some critical person and you could see that they fell in love with it.
zh: 在我参与的每一个重要产品中，都有这样一个时刻，当我们向某个关键人物展示它时，你可以看到他们爱上了它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sometimes they're literally pointing at the comps on the board, sometime you're in a meeting and they're just like, "God, I just love this."
zh: 有时他们真的指着板上的样稿，有时你在开会中他们就像，“天哪，我就是爱这个。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And for me, that was always the critical moment because I knew that design can't bring you this stuff into the world on its own.
zh: 对我来说，这总是关键时刻，因为我知道设计无法独自将这些东西带入世界。

speaker: Unknown
en: We can't raise this baby, we need the village, and we need the village to fall in love with the baby.
zh: 我们无法抚养这个婴儿，我们需要村庄，我们需要村庄爱上这个婴儿。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so until that happens, you're not really quite sure if this thing's going to take off or not.
zh: 所以在那发生之前，你不太确定这个东西是否会起飞。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it was always extremely important to me that you had a few key engineers and some product people fall in love with it so they could defend it and embrace it and enhance it and add to it.
zh: 所以对我来说，有一点关键工程师和一些产品人员爱上它总是极其重要的，这样他们就可以捍卫它、拥抱它、增强它并添加内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you got to bring them along at the very beginning.
zh: 你必须在一开始就带上他们。

speaker: Unknown
en: What I'm hearing there is there's a big part of just buy-in and then there's also just obviously more good ideas early are great.
zh: 我在这里听到的是，很大一部分是关于认同，然后显然早期有更多好想法也是很好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, sorry.
zh: 是的，抱歉。

speaker: Unknown
en: Buy-in doesn't feel quite right to me, because buy-in feels like, oh, I've come to agree with you.
zh: “认同”对我来说不太对劲，因为认同感觉像是，哦，我已经同意你了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's different from it's a part of me.
zh: 这与“它是我的一部分”是不同的。

speaker: Unknown
en: When I'm talking to teams, the thing I try to tell them is, I walk into the office every day with the idea that everyone that I work with is fundamentally a maker.
zh: 当我与团队交谈时，我试图告诉他们的是，我每天走进办公室时都带着这样一个想法，即我共事的每个人本质上都是创造者。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everybody in product design, engineering, we've all chosen these careers.
zh: 产品设计、工程领域的每个人，我们都选择了这些职业。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everybody's super smart, everybody's super ambitious.
zh: 每个人都超级聪明，每个人都超级有雄心。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everybody could have done a thousand other things, but they're choosing to spend their precious lifetime and creative energy creating software.
zh: 每个人本可以做一千件其他事情，但他们选择花费宝贵的生命和创造精力来创造软件。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I believe in my heart that they're all fundamentally makers.
zh: 所以我内心相信他们本质上都是创造者。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the thing that I know about makers is that they all want to make something they're proud of so they can take it home at the end of the day and show it to their parents and say, "Look at what I made at school with my friends today."
zh: 我对创造者了解的一点是，他们都想制造一些让他们自豪的东西，这样他们可以在一天结束时带回家给父母看，并说，“看今天我和朋友们在学校里做了什么。”

speaker: Unknown
en: That's the fundamental thing, and they're all doing it from their own different points of view and their own different incentives and mindsets, but they all at the end of the day want to make something they're proud of.
zh: 这是根本的事情，他们都是从自己不同的观点、不同的激励和心态出发做这件事，但在一天结束时，他们都想制造一些让他们自豪的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it's not a matter of getting their buy-in, it's a matter of them being a part of it.
zh: 所以这无关获得他们的认同，这是关于让他们成为其中的一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know, it's a part of their soul in a really deep, meaningful way.
zh: 我不知道，这是以一种真正深刻、有意义的方式成为他们灵魂的一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm not sure you can graph that onto somebody after the fact.
zh: 我不确定你是否能在事后将其附加到某个人身上。

speaker: Unknown
en: They kind of need to be there at the moment of inception, if you will.
zh: 如果你愿意的话，他们需要在受孕的那一刻就在场。

speaker: Unknown
en: Wow, that's a really beautiful answer.
zh: 哇，这是一个非常美丽的回答。

speaker: Unknown
en: I imagine for a lot of people hearing this, making every feature and product they build a part of their soul feels like a very high bar if they're building some kind of B2B SaaS software.
zh: 我想对于许多听众来说，让他们构建的每一个功能和产品都成为他们灵魂的一部分感觉像是一个非常高的标准，特别是如果他们正在构建某种 B2B SaaS 软件的话。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I guess just thoughts in just how much you should spend, how much time, how many resources, how deep you go on design for all these things you're building.
zh: 所以我想只是关于你应该投入多少，多少时间，多少资源，你在所有这些你正在构建的东西的设计上要深入到什么程度的想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: Say you're building some kind of, I don't know, expense management system or HRS thing, just like, what do you recommend people do with, in terms of just how far to go in design as a lever, as a differentiator maybe?
zh: 假设你正在构建某种，我不知道，费用管理系统或人力资源系统之类的东西，就像，你会建议人们怎么做，就设计作为一种杠杆，也许作为一种差异化因素而言，要走多远？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, inherent in your question is this assumption that design takes more time.
zh: 嗯，你的问题中隐含着这样一个假设，即设计需要更多时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I'm going to kind of reject that premise, because I don't think design takes more time.
zh: 所以我将某种程度上拒绝这个前提，因为我不认为设计需要更多时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think design exists.
zh: 我认为设计是存在的。

speaker: Unknown
en: There is going to be a design.
zh: 会有一个设计的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's whether it's going to be a good one or not.
zh: 问题在于它是否会是一个好的设计。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think there's things that you can do so that you're able to operate it at a quicker pace as design.
zh: 我认为你可以做一些事情，以便你能以更快的速度进行设计操作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Again, if you get the... We haven't talked about tenets yet, but we'll get to that in a moment.
zh: 同样，如果你得到……我们还没谈到信条，但我们稍后会谈到。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you kind of create a shared philosophical understanding of the product and what you're trying to do, you can go really fast because you're not asking the question of what should you do, you're asking the question of, what would this company with what we stand for do for this thing?
zh: 如果你建立了对产品的共同哲学理解以及你试图做的事情，你可以走得非常快，因为你不是在问“你应该做什么”这个问题，你是在问，“这个代表我们立场的公司会为这个东西做什么？”

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's a much easier question that's much smaller.
zh: 这是一个更容易得多、也小得多的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you look at the companies that have the largest design teams, they're often the companies that have the most ambiguous cultures and the most unclear design vision.
zh: 所以如果你看看那些拥有最大设计团队的公司，它们往往是那些拥有最模糊文化和最不明确设计愿景的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: When you go to companies that really know what they're doing and they're clear that this is who we are, this is what we stand for, the design teams are super small because they're not sitting there trying to do all these permutations with color and typography and ideas.
zh: 当你去那些真正知道自己在做什么的公司，他们很明确这就是我们是谁，这就是我们的立场，设计团队就非常小，因为他们没有坐在那里试图用颜色、排版和想法做所有这些排列组合。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're operating in a really narrow vein, because they know who they are.
zh: 他们在一个非常狭窄的范围内运作，因为他们知道他们是谁。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's very much like individuals.
zh: 这很像个人。

speaker: Unknown
en: When you're a teenager or a young adult, you can spend a lot of time trying to figure out what to wear because you haven't really sorted it out yet.
zh: 当你是青少年或年轻的成年人时，你可以花很多时间试图弄清楚该穿什么，因为你还没有真正理顺它。

speaker: Unknown
en: But by the time you get to be a little bit older, you've kind of got your personal style, and so dressing in the morning gets to be a lot easier.
zh: 但等你年纪稍大一点，你就有了自己的个人风格，所以早上穿衣服就变得容易多了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like at Pinterest.
zh: 就像在 Pinterest 那样。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was at Pinterest at a point when Pinterest wasn't quite sure who it was.
zh: 我曾在 Pinterest，那时的 Pinterest 还不太清楚自己是谁。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so when we were going to do an onboarding flow, we had to look at a really broad sweep of things, because we were trying to sort it out.
zh: 所以当我们准备做一个入职流程时，我们不得不审视非常广泛的一揽子事情，因为我们正在试图把它梳理清楚。

speaker: Unknown
en: But you had other places that knew what they were about, Apple's the key example there, we weren't trying to figure out what it was about.
zh: 但你还有其他一些知道自己核心是什么的地方，Apple 就是那里的关键例子，我们并不是试图弄清楚它关于什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: We were trying to figure out what was the apple way to do this particular thing, and so that moves a lot faster.
zh: 我们是试图弄清楚做这件事的 Apple 方式是什么，所以那进展得快得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I agree, look, having your soul at every little checkbox sounds like a high bar and in some ways it is.
zh: 我同意，听着，让每一个小复选框都有你的灵魂听起来门槛很高，在某种程度上确实是。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think you need to be able to back up and look at the product, maybe not at every state, but generally every six months or a year, you need to back up and ask yourself, am I proud of this?
zh: 我认为你需要能够退后一步审视产品，也许不是在每个阶段，但通常每六个月或一年，你需要退后一步问问自己，我为此感到骄傲吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is this something I am happy to be a part of?
zh: 这是我乐意参与的事情吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Do I believe in this?
zh: 我相信这个吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is it a representative of my best work given the circumstances I was in, which has limitations around time and resources and everything else, is this the best I could do or am I just sort of trying to get through the day I have other goals?
zh: 这是否代表了我在所处环境下做出的最好的工作，这有时间和资源等等方面的限制，这是我能做的最好的吗，还是我只是试图熬过这一天我有其他目标？

speaker: Unknown
en: So let's actually follow the thread of design tenets and principles.
zh: 所以让我们真正顺着设计信条和原则的线索来谈。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is something I've heard about you, that you're a big fan of design tenets versus design principles.
zh: 这是关于你的一件事我听说过的，你是设计信条对比设计原则的超级粉丝。

speaker: Unknown
en: What is the difference?
zh: 区别是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Why is this so important?
zh: 为什么这如此重要？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, so look, there's whole websites dedicated to design principles, and if you go and you read it, you'll see a lot of principles like simple, clear, beautiful, fast, secure.
zh: 是的，所以听着，有专门致力于设计原则的整个网站，如果你去读它，你会看到很多像简单、清晰、美观、快速、安全的原则。

speaker: Unknown
en: You'll hear these words and all these words are great.
zh: 你会听到这些词，所有这些词都很棒。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, obviously I have nothing against any of these words, but they're not useful as decision-making tools because nobody would ever argue the opposite.
zh: 我的意思是，显然我对这些词没有任何异议，但它们作为决策工具没有用处，因为没有人会争论相反的一面。

speaker: Unknown
en: Nobody ever sat in a meeting and said, "Oh, forget clear.
zh: 从来没有人坐在会议上说，“噢，忘掉清晰吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's try to make it as confusing as possible."
zh: 让我们试着让它尽可能令人困惑。”

speaker: Unknown
en: So the idea of clear, it's nice to have out there as, I don't know, sort of a platitude to move towards, but I just don't think it helps you make decisions.
zh: 所以清晰这个概念，把它摆在那里很好，作为某种要去追求的陈词滥调，但我只是认为它无助于你做决策。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so tenets are really decision-making tools and it's sort of like... A classic one is paper versus plastic.
zh: 所以信条真的是决策工具，它有点像……一个经典的例子是纸对塑料。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just too complicated to reconsider that every time you're at the grocery store.
zh: 每次你在杂货店都要重新考虑这个太复杂了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you sort of make a rule for yourself and you're just a paper person or a plastic person, you move on from there.
zh: 所以你给自己定个规则，你就是一个纸袋人士或塑料袋人士，然后你就从那里继续。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it's sort of that at scale.
zh: 所以这在规模化上也是类似的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the story comes from when they were starting to work on Keynotes, apparently the guy who was responsible for originating Keynote went to Steve and said, "How should we think about Keynote?"
zh: 这个故事来自于当他们开始开发 Keynote 时，显然负责发起 Keynote 的人去找 Steve 并说，“我们应该如何看待 Keynote？”

speaker: Unknown
en: And Steve said, "I want you to keep three things in mind.
zh: Steve 说，“我希望你记住三件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: One is it should be difficult to make ugly presentations.
zh: 第一，应该很难做出丑陋的演示文稿。

speaker: Unknown
en: Two, you should focus on cinematic quality transitions.
zh: 第二，你应该关注电影画质的转场。

speaker: Unknown
en: And three, you should optimize for innovation over PowerPoint compatibility."
zh: 第三，你应该为创新而不是 PowerPoint 兼容性做优化。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you take that last one in particular, if he hadn't kind of said, we're going to go this way instead of that way, that team would've spent the next 10 years gouging each other's eyes out over whether they should try to go for PowerPoint compatibility or innovation.
zh: 如果你特别看最后一点，如果他某种程度上没有说，我们要走这条路而不是那条路，那个团队会在接下来的十年里为了是应该追求 PowerPoint 兼容性还是创新而互相挖眼珠子。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so when I was at ThoughtSpot, I realized pretty early on that I wasn't going to be able to have any sort of command and control over everything that was going to happen in the product.
zh: 所以当我在 ThoughtSpot 时，我很早就意识到我无法对产品中发生的所有事情有任何形式的命令和控制。

speaker: Unknown
en: There was too many people involved, too many engineering teams, most of them were in India.
zh: 涉及的人太多了，工程团队太多了，其中大多数在印度。

speaker: Unknown
en: I needed to move from a mindset of control to one of choreography.
zh: 我需要从控制的心态转变为编舞的心态。

speaker: Unknown
en: I needed to try to set the culture and set certain design tenets that everyone could internalize and follow and hopefully then make the right decisions in that groove, if you will.
zh: 我需要试图确立文化并设定某些设计信条，让每个人都能内化并遵循，然后希望在那个节奏中做出正确的决定，如果你愿意这么说的话。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we had three, I think you can't have more than three or four because you need everybody to memorize them.
zh: 所以我们有三条，我认为你不能超过三四条，因为你需要每个人记住它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: They can't be consulting a handbook.
zh: 他们不能去查阅手册。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, one of them was documentation is a failure state.
zh: 所以，其中一条是文档是一种失败状态。

speaker: Unknown
en: In enterprise companies, a lot of times people think, "Oh, we'll just put it in the manual.
zh: 在企业公司里，很多时候人们认为，“噢，我们把它放在手册里就行。

speaker: Unknown
en: It'll be part of the training."
zh: 它会成为培训的一部分。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And I would constantly be coming back and go, "Stop it.
zh: 而我会不断地回来并说，“停下。

speaker: Unknown
en: Nobody wants to learn our software.
zh: 没有人想学习我们的软件。

speaker: Unknown
en: Nobody cares.
zh: 没有人在乎。

speaker: Unknown
en: We are just one more browser tab in a world of browser tabs.
zh: 我们只是浏览器标签世界里的又一个标签页。

speaker: Unknown
en: We are not this user's complete world.
zh: 我们不是这个用户的完整世界。

speaker: Unknown
en: They do not want to learn this stuff."
zh: 他们不想学习这些东西。”

speaker: Unknown
en: Documentation's a failure state.
zh: 文档是一种失败状态。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe we can't always avoid it, but we should do everything we can to simplify things so you can figure it out in the context of the product.
zh: 也许我们不能总是避免它，但我们应该尽一切可能简化事情，这样你就能在产品的上下文中弄明白它。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's number one.
zh: 这是第一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Number two is every interaction should start simple and the users should have to opt into complexity.
zh: 第二点是每次交互都应该从简单开始，用户应该选择加入复杂性。

speaker: Unknown
en: So our main competitor at the time was Tableau.
zh: 所以我们当时的主要竞争对手是 Tableau。

speaker: Unknown
en: Tableau started with complexity.
zh: Tableau 始于复杂性。

speaker: Unknown
en: That was their whole value prop is like, "We're a super powerful tool.
zh: 这就是他们的全部价值主张，比如，“我们是一个超级强大的工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: We can do all sorts of stuff."
zh: 我们可以做各种各样的事情。”

speaker: Unknown
en: So when you sit down at Tableau, it feels like you're flying the space shuttle.
zh: 所以当你坐在 Tableau 面前时，感觉就像你在驾驶航天飞机。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you're a professional data analyst, that's great.
zh: 如果你是一名专业数据分析师，那就太好了。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's the kind of tool you wanted.
zh: 那就是你想要的工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: That wasn't what ThoughtSpot was about.
zh: 那不是 ThoughtSpot 的宗旨。

speaker: Unknown
en: We were trying to take data analytics into the hands of what I call mere mortals, also known as business users, people who didn't live in breathe this stuff every day.
zh: 我们试图将数据分析交到我称之为凡人的人手中，也就是所谓的业务用户，那些不是每天以此为生的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: So our goal with them was they could sit down and it was an approachable piece of software and they could turn on all the bells and whistles and power if they wanted it, so that was the second one.
zh: 因此我们要为他们的目标是，他们坐下来时，面对的是一个亲切易懂的软件，如果他们愿意，可以开启所有的铃声和口哨以及强大的功能，所以那是第二个。

speaker: Unknown
en: Start simple, let the users opt into complexity.
zh: 从简单开始，让用户选择加入复杂性。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the third one was the entire product should look and feel like it came from a single mind.
zh: 第三个是整个产品的外观和感觉应该像出自同一个头脑。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this was a tenet to try to combat the natural tendency of enterprise companies to really fragment because you have all these different teams working on their incentive to work just on their little piece.
zh: 这是一个旨在对抗企业公司自然分散倾向的宗旨，因为你有所有这些不同的团队在为了他们的激励而努力工作，只做他们的一小块。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so they think about what's right for them and they don't back up to look at the whole thing.
zh: 因此他们考虑什么对他们来说是正确的，而不是退后一步来看看整体。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we had this tenet, the whole thing should look and feel like it came from a single mind to just try to remind people, how does this fit into the whole system?
zh: 所以我们有这个宗旨，整个东西的外观和感觉应该像出自同一个头脑，只是为了提醒人们，这如何适应整个系统？

speaker: Unknown
en: And sometimes we need to go along and do things that work for the product that don't necessarily work quite the way we might want them to for our feature.
zh: 有时我们需要继续前行，做一些对产品有效的事情，这些事情不一定完全符合我们对我们功能的期望。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so those tenets were all... Again, they were all decision-making tools.
zh: 所以这些宗旨都是……再说一次，它们都是决策工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when we would have design debates, we could just come back to this, wait, are we actually starting simple and forcing them to opt into complexity or are we doing something else here?
zh: 当我们进行设计辩论时，我们可以回到这里，等等，我们实际上是开始简单并强迫他们选择加入复杂性，还是我们在做别的事情？

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's kind of this implication in this discussion about tenets is that you need to be very opinionated.
zh: 所以关于宗旨的讨论中隐含的意思是，你需要非常有主见。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a clear here's what's in and here's what's out.
zh: 这里清楚地界定了什么在里面，什么在外面。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is there anything more along those lines and are there other tenet examples you could share to give people some inspiration as they think about their potential tenets?
zh: 还有其他类似的内容吗？你能分享其他宗旨的例子吗，给人们一些启发，让他们思考自己潜在的宗旨？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's very context specific, so it's a little bit like what are your tenets for parenting?
zh: 这非常依赖于上下文，所以有点像你的育儿宗旨是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a very specific personal type thing that's germane to your particular context.
zh: 这是一个非常具体的个人类型的事情，与你的特定背景有关。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I'm not sure if I have a lot of other examples, and I haven't heard this used by a lot of other companies, so I haven't been able to add a bunch of stuff.
zh: 所以我不确定我是否有其他很多例子，而且我没有听到很多其他公司使用这个词，所以我没能添加一堆东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: We tried to come out with tenets for individual features and we had trouble with that.
zh: 我们试图为个别功能制定宗旨，但我们在那方面遇到了困难。

speaker: Unknown
en: It felt like they operated at sort of the design strategy level.
zh: 感觉它们是在设计策略层面运作的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I just think that varies dramatically from company to company.
zh: 而且我认为这在公司与公司之间差异很大。

speaker: Unknown
en: What I would look for is if you're a design leader or a product leader, try to pay attention to what are the debates that we keep having over and over where people kind of seem to be digging in and things sort of seem to be bifurcating into two camps.
zh: 如果你是设计负责人或产品负责人，你要关注的是我们要反复进行的辩论，人们似乎在坚守立场，事情似乎分化成两个阵营。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then is there something we can do where we just have that debate once and for all, we decide as an organization, we're going left instead of right, and you're absolutely correct.
zh: 然后我们能不能做点什么，让我们一劳永逸地进行那次辩论，我们作为一个组织决定，我们向左而不是向右，而你绝对正确。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to be opinionated, but that's how you're going to win.
zh: 你必须有主见，但这就是你获胜的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's no unopinionated software that's been successful.
zh: 没有哪款没有主见的软件取得了成功。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to have a point of view.
zh: 你必须有一个观点。

speaker: Unknown
en: The question is, what's it going to be?
zh: 问题是，它会是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: So I'd say practically just try to look for places where it seems the team's having the same debate over and over and have it once, get it done, and put it behind you.
zh: 所以我想说的是，实际上只是试着寻找那些团队似乎在反复进行同样辩论的地方，进行一次，把它完成，然后把它抛在脑后。

speaker: Unknown
en: And make it a tenet.
zh: 并把它变成一个宗旨。

speaker: Unknown
en: And why is the word tenet versus principle so important?
zh: 为什么宗旨这个词比原则这个词如此重要？

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know.
zh: 我不知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: I settled on tenet.
zh: 我选择了宗旨。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'd have to go look up the definition.
zh: 我得去查一下定义。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was trying to differentiate it from principles because I think principles are just... I describe principles as sort of Applehood & Motherpie.
zh: 我试图将它与原则区分开来，因为我认为原则只是……我将原则描述为某种像 Applehood & Mother Pie 的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Again, they're just not something people are going to argue over.
zh: 再说一次，它们只是人们不会争论的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I didn't think it was wise to try to co-op that word and change how people think about it so much as I might be more successful just coming up with a different word altogether.
zh: 所以我认为试图占用这个词并改变人们对它的看法是不明智的，不如我完全想出一个不同的词可能会更成功。

speaker: Unknown
en: Makes sense.
zh: 有道理。
