speaker: Unknown
en: I want to zoom out a little bit and another theme that came up a bunch when I ask people about you and how you think is that you have a really strong feeling that building great product and building successful product is a moral obligation of people that are in tech.
zh: 我想稍微拉开一点视角,当我问及你以及你的思维方式时,另一个频繁出现的主题是,你有一种强烈的感受,即构建伟大的产品和构建成功的产品是技术人员的一项道德义务。

speaker: Unknown
en: Talk about why you feel that way and what that even means.
zh: 谈谈为什么你有这种感觉,以及这到底是什么意思。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, look, the example I use mostly is if you go to an airport and you look around, you'll see a lot of people using their phone to navigate that system.
zh: 好吧,听着,我主要用的例子是,如果你去机场,四处看看,你会看到很多人用手机在那个系统中导航。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're trying to figure out where their gate is, what time their flight's on, whether or not... Can they pull up their boarding pass, et cetera.
zh: 他们试图弄清楚他们的登机口在哪里,他们的航班是几点,是否能拉出他们的登机牌,等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: And just watch people, watch their faces, watch the level of confusion and frustration.
zh: 就观察这些人,看他们的脸,看那种困惑和挫折的程度。

speaker: Unknown
en: Some of them are tech superheroes like you and me and most of your listeners, but a lot of them are just mere mortals and they're not living and breathing this stuff all the time.
zh: 其中一些人是像你我以及你的大多数听众那样的技术超级英雄,但很多人只是凡人,他们不是一直都在呼吸和沉浸在这些东西里。

speaker: Unknown
en: And a lot of times they're super frustrated and then take that and scale it out to their entire day.
zh: 很多时候他们超级沮丧,然后把这种情绪放大到他们的一整天中。

speaker: Unknown
en: And almost everyone living in a modern economy now is going to have hundreds of interactions with the phone or with a computer.
zh: 现在,几乎每个生活在现代经济体中的人都会与手机或电脑进行数百次的互动。

speaker: Unknown
en: And a lot of those interactions are going to be consequential.
zh: 其中很多互动将是具有重要后果的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Unfortunately, a lot of those interactions are not going to be great.
zh: 不幸的是,其中很多互动不会是伟大的。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're going to be confusing and frustrating.
zh: 它们将是令人困惑和沮丧的。

speaker: Unknown
en: When I'm speaking to live audiences, I often ask people, okay, please raise your hand if you've had a frustrating or confusing experience with software in the last month?
zh: 当我面对现场观众演讲时,我经常问人们,好的,如果你在过去一个月里有过令人沮丧或令人困惑的软件体验,请举手?

speaker: Unknown
en: And obviously every hand goes up.
zh: 显然每只手都举起来了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, how about so far this week?
zh: 好的,那么到本周为止呢?

speaker: Unknown
en: Most all hands stay up.
zh: 大多数手仍然举着。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm like, okay, how about so far today?
zh: 我说,好的,那么到今天为止呢?

speaker: Unknown
en: And most of the hands stay up, and it's often that I speak in the morning, I'm like, okay, everybody's had a frustrating experience with software and it's 10 o'clock in the morning.
zh: 大多数手仍然举着,而且经常是我在早上演讲,我会说,好的,每个人都经历过令人沮丧的软件体验,而现在是早上 10 点。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a problem, people, because each one of those interactions, it takes a little bit of energy away from you and it ramps your frustration just a little bit.
zh: 这是一个问题,人们,因为每一次这样的互动都会从你身上带走一点能量,并且只是稍微加剧了你的挫败感。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the bummer about software, both for the audience and for the creators is that it's an anonymous medium.
zh: 关于软件的令人遗憾之处,无论对观众还是创作者来说,它都是一种匿名媒介。

speaker: Unknown
en: Nobody gets to see who's making these things.
zh: 没有人能看到是谁在制造这些东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: You and I together, we might be able to name six designers that have worked on products we care about.
zh: 你和我在一起,也许能说出六个设计师的名字,他们曾在我们关心的产品上工作过。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the only reason we could do that is because a designer and I know a bunch of them.
zh: 我们能这样做的唯一原因是因为我是一个设计师,而且我认识其中很多人。

speaker: Unknown
en: By yourself, I'd be surprised if you could name more than a handful.
zh: 靠你自己的话,如果你能说出超过几个名字,我会感到惊讶。

speaker: Unknown
en: And again, we work in tech.
zh: 而且,我们要再说一次,我们在技术行业工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you think about the billions of people out there that don't work in tech, to them, these products are just these crazy faceless things created by a bunch of people who knows where, and these products are causing them untold amounts of frustration and confusion, and it just takes away from their life quality.
zh: 所以如果你想想外面那几十亿不在技术行业工作的人,对他们来说,这些产品只是这些疯狂的无脸事物,由一群不知道在哪里的人创造出来的,而这些产品给他们造成了难以言说的挫折和困惑,这只会降低他们的生活质量。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think we have an obligation as product people to put that emotional energy back into people's lives.
zh: 我认为我们作为产品人员有义务把这种情感能量回馈到人们的生活中。

speaker: Unknown
en: They don't want to try to figure out how to navigate our login screens or go through our onboarding process, they just want to get home and spend time with their families and pet their dogs and have a nice dinner.
zh: 他们不想试图弄清楚如何浏览我们的登录界面或经历我们的入职流程,他们只是想回家,花时间和家人在一起,遛遛狗,吃顿美好的晚餐。

speaker: Unknown
en: I just think every time we make a demand on the audience, that's a failure on our part.
zh: 我只是认为,每一次我们向观众提出要求,这都意味着我们的一次失败。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I do think it comes... I cast it in a moral way, and I talk about it that way because I don't think many people working in the industry understand the scale of what they're doing, again, because it's an anonymous field.
zh: 所以我确实认为这源自……我把它以道德的方式来构建,并且我用那种方式谈论它,因为我认为在这个行业工作的许多人并不理解他们所做事情的规模,同样,因为这是一个匿名领域。

speaker: Unknown
en: We never see anybody on the other side of the glass.
zh: 我们从未看到玻璃另一侧的任何人。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think with this podcast, it'll go out to, I don't know, hundreds of thousands of people.
zh: 但我认为通过这个播客,它将传达给,我不知道,几十万人。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you and I saw all the people that will potentially listen to this in one place, we would think to ourselves, oh my goodness, that's like a lot of people.
zh: 如果你和我看到所有可能会听这个节目的人在一个地方,我们会对自己说,天哪,那是很多人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we might think of it differently.
zh: 我们可能会以不同的方式看待它。

speaker: Unknown
en: We might behave differently.
zh: 我们可能会有不同的表现。

speaker: Unknown
en: My team at Apple, but also my friends that are working at Facebook or Google or wherever, it's very hard to really understand that they're creating something in Figma on their computer that's going to be interacted with by billions of people, thousands and thousands of times.
zh: 我在苹果的团队,还有我在 Facebook 或 Google 或任何地方的朋友,很难真正理解他们正在电脑上的 Figma 中创造某种将被数十亿人互动成千上万次的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you lose sight of that I think just, I don't know, you get sloppy and disrespectful is the wrong word, but I think you just lose sight of how much impact you're having on other people.
zh: 如果你忽略了这一点,我认为只是,我不知道,你会变得草率和不尊重是错误的词,但我认为你只是忘记了你对他人的影响有多大。

speaker: Unknown
en: Wow, that's really inspiring.
zh: 哇,这真的很鼓舞人心。

speaker: Unknown
en: That makes me want to build products and make them awesome.
zh: 这让我想去构建产品并使它们变得很棒。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's so much power to that.
zh: 这其中有很大的力量。

speaker: Unknown
en: What this makes me think about a little bit is kind of random, but when I see someone click and watch one of my podcast videos on YouTube, I'm like, wow, that's one person that's going to spend their time watching this thing.
zh: 这让我想到的一点点有点随机,但当我在 YouTube 上看到有人点击并观看我的一个播客视频时,我会想,哇,有一个人要花时间观看这个东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Wow, I really want to make... It gives me more motivation to make these even better and better.
zh: 哇,我真的想要制作……这给了我更多的动力去把这些东西做得越来越好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, look, I think you have to find ways to go... You have to find where you go out of your way to see people using software in real time.
zh: 是的,听着,我认为你必须找到方法去……你必须找到你特意去看人们实时使用软件的方法。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've worked on products that have been used by billions of people.
zh: 我曾参与过数十亿人使用的产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: I have friends who have touched billions of people.
zh: 我有朋友接触过数十亿人。

speaker: Unknown
en: None of us ever get to see anybody use this stuff in the wild, in their natural state.
zh: 我们从未见过有人在野外,在自然状态下使用这些东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe we see them in a lab or something like that, but I've never seen anybody just randomly using even Pinterest.
zh: 也许我们在实验室或类似的地方看到他们,但我从未见过有人只是随意地使用即使是 Pinterest。

speaker: Unknown
en: But there's ways that you can go and as a creator, as a maker, you can go and watch people using software in the wild.
zh: 但是有一些方法你可以去,作为一个创作者,作为一个制造者,你可以去观察人们在野外使用软件。

speaker: Unknown
en: So just go observe people going through self-checkout at Target, which is the best self-checkout I've ever seen.
zh: 所以就去观察人们在 Target 进行自助结账,这是我所见过的最好的自助结账。

speaker: Unknown
en: Go watch that, then go watch it at some other grocery store where it's not as great and really notice what happens with people.
zh: 去看那个,然后去其他一些不那么好的杂货店看,并真正注意人们身上发生了什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: Much to my kids' frustration when their friends are over, I often grab their friend's phone and just sort of flip through it to try to understand how people are organizing their home screens and which apps they use.
zh: 让我孩子们沮丧的是,当他们的朋友过来时,我经常抓过他们朋友的手机,只是翻阅一下,试图了解人们是如何组织他们的主屏幕以及他们使用哪些应用程序。

speaker: Unknown
en: And maybe there's something in there that I haven't seen, I'll ask them what that is and ask them to give me a tour of it.
zh: 也许里面有什么东西我没看到，我会问他们那是什么，并请他们带我看一看。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think we're living in a time where people don't do so many usability studies, so a lot of folks get pretty far into their careers without ever having watched mere mortals actually use software.
zh: 我认为我们生活在一个人们不做太多可用性研究的时代，所以很多人在职业生涯中走了很远，却从未观察过凡人真正使用软件的情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: Instead, we're relying on metrics and stuff, which I sort of joked that relying on metrics to understand what's happening at the user level is like looking at raw data from a radio telescope instead of just going out inside and looking at the night sky.
zh: 相反，我们依赖指标之类的东西，我开玩笑说，依赖指标来理解用户层面发生的事情，就像查看射电望远镜的原始数据，而不是直接走到外面去看夜空。

speaker: Unknown
en: You got to find a way to watch the audience.
zh: 你必须找到一种方法去观察受众。

speaker: Unknown
en: Filmmakers can go to a theater, they can watch people, understand stuff.
zh: 电影制作人可以去剧院，他们可以观察人们，理解事物。

speaker: Unknown
en: Comedians can go to a comedy club, they can start to develop an intuition about why people laugh.
zh: 喜剧演员可以去喜剧俱乐部，他们可以开始建立一种关于人们为什么笑的直觉。

speaker: Unknown
en: None of us have an obvious way to go watch people use software, so we don't really understand how humans process what's happening on the screen.
zh: 我们没有一个明显的方法去观察人们使用软件，所以我们并不真正理解人类如何处理屏幕上发生的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you have to just find ways to do that.
zh: 你必须找到方法去这样做。

speaker: Unknown
en: And fortunately, software is everywhere.
zh: 幸运的是，软件无处不在。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not just desktop or mobile software.
zh: 这不仅仅是桌面或移动软件。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, there's ATM machines, there's ticketing kiosks, there's point of sale systems everywhere.
zh: 我是说，有 ATM 机，有售票亭，到处都有销售点系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, go watch somebody over 70 fumble with a chip card insert or watch somebody try to figure out Apple Pay.
zh: 我是说，去看看 70 岁以上的人笨拙地插入芯片卡，或者看看有人试图弄懂 Apple Pay。

speaker: Unknown
en: And these are pretty seamless experiences and still there's cognitive friction in all this stuff.
zh: 这些都是非常无缝的体验，但在所有这些事情中仍然存在认知摩擦。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just go rent a car and notice how long it takes you to figure out what the heck is going on with the dashboard.
zh: 就去租一辆车，注意你弄清楚仪表盘到底是怎么回事需要花多长时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's lots of opportunities to try to develop that intuition of how people navigate the human computer interaction, and we need to find ways to do that.
zh: 有很多机会可以尝试建立那种关于人们如何导航人机交互的直觉，我们需要找到方法来做到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: An important element of what you're describing here, which I think maybe people miss, is that you're talking about just any software, not your own product, in order to start building your sense of taste and gut feeling for what-
zh: 你在这里描述的一个重要元素，我想人们可能会忽略，就是你说的是任何软件，而不是你自己的产品，以便开始建立你对什么是有效的、什么是无效的品味和直觉。

speaker: Unknown
en: Building your sense of taste and gut feeling for what works and doesn't work.
zh: 建立你对什么是有效的、什么是无效的品味和直觉。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I had a guest on recently, Guillermo Rauch from Vercel, founder of Vercel, and he had a really great phrase of something they do at their company.
zh: 我最近有一位嘉宾，Vercel 的创始人 Guillermo Rauch，他在他们的公司有一个非常好的说法。

speaker: Unknown
en: They have this kind of mission of exposure hours.
zh: 他们有一种「接触小时」的使命。

speaker: Unknown
en: Increase your exposure hours to people using our product.
zh: 增加你接触使用我们产品的人的时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you can extrapolate that to any product.
zh: 然后你可以将其推断到任何产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, well there's using your product, but I always think when you're watching somebody use your product, you come into it with a psychological bias that makes it hard for you to really see what's going on.
zh: 是的，嗯，有使用你的产品，但我一直认为，当你看着某人使用你的产品时，你会带着一种心理偏见进入，这让你很难真正看到发生了什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's something about just understanding the audience and how they process information on a screen, not your product.
zh: 所以只是理解受众以及他们如何处理屏幕上的信息，而不是你的产品，这有一点门道。

speaker: Unknown
en: At one point when I was redesigning a checkout system, we did what I called a reality check, which was we held a traditional usability style exercise in a lab and all that sort of stuff, but we had the subjects come through and go through checkout in other products.
zh: 有一次当我重新设计一个结账系统时，我们做了我所谓的「现实检验」，就是我们在实验室举行了一场传统的可用性练习和所有这类事情，但我们让受试者来并通过其他产品进行结账。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we watched them go through eBay and Williams-Sonoma and Amazon or something like that.
zh: 所以我们观察他们通过 eBay、Williams-Sonoma 和 Amazon 或类似的东西进行结账。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we learned a ton about checkout, about what was important to them, how it turns out ship quote is almost as important as price.
zh: 我们对结账、对他们来说什么重要了解了很多，结果发现运费报价几乎和价格一样重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: Things that if we had been watching them use our own product, I'm not sure we would've picked up on, because we would've been sitting there yelling at them to click on the button.
zh: 如果我们观察他们使用我们自己的产品，我不确定我们会发现这些事情，因为我们会坐在那里对他们大喊点击那个按钮。

speaker: Unknown
en: Or we would've had a bias and wanting to see the positive things.
zh: 或者我们会有一种偏见，想要看到积极的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Whereas, if you just watch people that are using adjacent products could be super useful.
zh: 然而，如果你只是观察使用相邻产品的人，可能会非常有用。

speaker: Unknown
en: And again, we work in a medium, software is a medium, and we need to understand our medium in the same way.
zh: 而且，我们在一个媒介中工作，软件是一个媒介，我们需要以同样的方式理解我们的媒介。

speaker: Unknown
en: Again, musicians go to concerts, filmmakers go to movies, comedians go to comic clubs.
zh: 同样，音乐家去听音乐会，电影制作人去看电影，喜剧演员去喜剧俱乐部。

speaker: Unknown
en: When do people like you and I go watch people just use software?
zh: 像你我这样的人什么时候去观察人们使用软件？

speaker: Unknown
en: Where do we develop that intuition?
zh: 我们在哪里培养那种直觉？

speaker: Unknown
en: And unfortunately I think you have to go out of your way to do it.
zh: 不幸的是，我认为你必须特意去做。

speaker: Unknown
en: Talk about more about this idea that software is a medium.
zh: 多谈谈「软件是一个媒介」这个想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is something that came up a bunch also in conversations with folks that have worked with you, that this is something that you believe.
zh: 这是在和你共事过的人的对话中经常出现的事情，这是你相信的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, you're so good with the research, Lenny.
zh: 是的，你很擅长做研究，Lenny。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, look, so I left Pinterest in 2016, sorry, 2016.
zh: 是的，听着，所以我在 2016 年离开了 Pinterest，抱歉，是 2016 年。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I didn't have anything lined up so I had some time to myself and I was driving up and down the peninsula here in Silicon Valley meeting with other design leaders and just sort of commiserating with people.
zh: 我没有安排任何事情，所以我有一段自己的时间，我在硅谷这里沿着半岛来回开车，与其他设计领导者会面，只是有点与人们共情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you may remember there was a very consequential presidential election in the United States in 2016 and there was some impression that social media had had a significant impact on that election.
zh: 你可能记得，2016 年美国有一场非常重要的总统选举，有一种印象是社交媒体对那次选举产生了重大影响。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I was kind of driving around Silicon Valley and I was just sort of wondering what the heck happened.
zh: 所以我在硅谷到处开车，我只是想知道到底发生了什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: I moved here in 1990 when the hippie ethos that was really at the core of Silicon Valley, and the hippie ethos was still very visible, it was very much a part of what was interesting to me about the valley when I moved here.
zh: 我在 1990 年搬到这里，当时嬉皮士精神是硅谷的核心，嬉皮士精神仍然非常明显，它是我在这里时我觉得硅谷有趣的一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: But 2016 is a long time later and that hippie ethos had gotten pretty quiet.
zh: 但 2016 年是很久以后了，那种嬉皮士精神已经变得相当安静了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I was listening to a podcast about the history of Silicon Valley by a Stanford group.
zh: 所以我在听一个斯坦福团队制作的关于硅谷历史的播客。

speaker: Unknown
en: The podcast was called Raw Data, and it was season two.
zh: 这个播客叫 Raw Data，是第二季。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it starts off with an episode called A Monument to a Dead Child, which is about Stanford University, and it ends with Zuckerberg's testimony in front of Congress.
zh: 它以一集叫「死难儿童纪念碑」的节目开始，是关于斯坦福大学的，最后以扎克伯格在国会前的证词结束。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in the middle of that, they start talking about the counterculture revolution in the late 1960s in San Francisco and elsewhere.
zh: 在这中间，他们开始谈论 1960 年代末在旧金山和其他地方的反文化革命。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they quote this book by a guy named Fred Turner, I think it is, the book's called From Counterculture to Cyberculture.
zh: 他们引用了一个叫 Fred Turner 的人的一本书，我想是的，这本书叫《从反文化到赛博文化》。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he has this quote that is, "you have to ask why it is personal computing got started in Northern California in the late 1960s when at the time every major tech company in the country was on the East Coast.
zh: 他有一句话是，「你必须问为什么，为什么个人计算是在 1960 年代末在北加州开始的，当时这个国家的每一家主要科技公司都在东海岸。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the answer is because there was a very small group of people in and around Stanford University that saw software as a new form of media on par with movies, music and books."
zh: 答案是因为斯坦福大学周围有很小的一群人，他们将软件视为一种与电影、音乐和书籍同等地位的新型媒体。」

speaker: Unknown
en: And when I heard that, all of a sudden I went, wait a second, boom.
zh: 当我听到那个时，我突然觉得，等一下，轰。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is why I do this.
zh: 这就是我做这个的原因。

speaker: Unknown
en: I am fundamentally a maker.
zh: 我本质上是一个创作者。

speaker: Unknown
en: In high school I was a photographer, in college I was going to be a filmmaker, after college I went to music school.
zh: 高中时我是个摄影师，大学时我打算成为一名电影制作人，大学毕业后我去了音乐学校。

speaker: Unknown
en: After music school I started a graphic design studio.
zh: 音乐学校毕业后，我开了一家平面设计工作室。

speaker: Unknown
en: I am a maker.
zh: 我是一个创作者。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I realized looking back, I was just hunting for my medium.
zh: 而且我回首往事，意识到我只是在寻找我的媒介。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it took me until I was 27 to find software as my medium.
zh: 我直到 27 岁才找到软件作为我的媒介。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like, oh, I'm a maker that designs software.
zh: 就像是，哦，我是一个设计软件的创作者。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then when I heard that software as a medium, that whole concept of what I'd been doing with my life and who I was about, it just sort of all came together really quickly.
zh: 然后当我听到软件作为一种媒介时，我这一生一直在做的事情以及我是谁的那个整体概念，就像真的非常快地凝聚在了一起。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I realized, oh, I am into software because software makes me feel a certain way when it's working well.
zh: 我意识到，哦，我投身软件是因为当软件运行良好时，它让我感觉很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what I find so troubling now is that a lot of time it's not working that way.
zh: 我现在觉得非常困扰的是，很多时候它并没有那样运行。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I remember the first time I saw a computer, probably a lot of people on listening to the show can remember maybe the first time they saw a desktop computer, probably the first time they saw a pension zoom on a phone.
zh: 我记得我第一次看到电脑，可能很多听这个节目的人都能记得他们第一次看到台式电脑，可能是第一次在手机上看到 pension zoom 的时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: You remember all that stuff.
zh: 你记得所有那些东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was just freaking magic man.
zh: 那简直是见鬼的魔法，伙计。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was the future.
zh: 那就是未来。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was so cool, and it just felt like the most amazing aurora borealis, or sunrise, or whatever.
zh: 那太酷了，感觉就像是最神奇极光，或者日出，或者什么似的。

speaker: Unknown
en: There was a sense of awe and wonder that filled me and probably a lot of listeners, that's probably the thing that motivated you to be in the field.
zh: 有一种敬畏和惊奇的感觉充满了我也可能充满了许多听众，那可能就是激励你进入这个领域的原因。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I realized software is a medium because there's an emotional component to it.
zh: 所以我意识到软件是一种媒介，因为它有一个情感成分。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like a hammer and saw, they're not really pulling out an emotion for me.
zh: 像锤子和锯子，它们真的不会给我唤起一种情感。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe there's some, if you're a carpenter, but I don't naturally have an emotion with kitchen tools or things that I think even more sophisticated tools like calculators and pulleys, I still don't have an emotional response to them.
zh: 也许有一些，如果你是个木匠，但我对厨房工具或者我认为更复杂的工具如计算器和滑轮天生没有情感，我仍然对它们没有情感反应。

speaker: Unknown
en: But every piece of software I have an emotional response to.
zh: 但我对每一个软件都有情感反应。

speaker: Unknown
en: I either feel confused or empowered.
zh: 我要么感到困惑，要么感到赋能。

speaker: Unknown
en: I feel like my world's gotten bigger or my world's gotten smaller.
zh: 我觉得我的世界变大了，或者我的世界变小了。

speaker: Unknown
en: They all have an emotional component.
zh: 它们都有一个情感成分。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think once you realize and accept that, then you can say, oh, there is an emotional component to what we're doing with this product.
zh: 我认为一旦你意识到并接受这一点，你就可以说，哦，我们要用这个产品做的事情有一个情感成分。

speaker: Unknown
en: I could just leave that to chance, which is what most people do, or I could try to be conscious of it and we could try to bring that into our conception of what the product's about and try to be purposeful in the emotion we're trying to elicit from the user.
zh: 我可以把它交给运气，这是大多数人所做的，或者我可以尝试有意识地对待它，我们可以尝试把它带入我们对产品概念的理解中，并尝试有意识地处理我们试图从用户那里引出的情感。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that's where design and particularly visual design can have a huge impact.
zh: 我认为这就是设计，尤其是视觉设计可以产生巨大影响的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: So again, in many conversations that I'd have in design reviews, some executive would go, "I don't know, ultimately this just kind of comes down to a matter of opinion."
zh: 所以再次说，在我在设计评审中进行的许多对话中，一些高管会说，“我不知道，归根结底这只是观点问题。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And I was always like, "no, it does not.
zh: 而我总是说，“不，不是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Whether we choose blue or red is going to elicit a certain emotional response from the user.
zh: 我们选择蓝色还是红色会引发用户特定的情感反应。

speaker: Unknown
en: What is it we want them to feel?
zh: 我们想让他们感觉到什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: And then let's make sure that we design something visually that evokes that emotion."
zh: 然后让我们确保我们在视觉上设计一些能唤起那种情感的东西。”

speaker: Unknown
en: So again, I think once you really get your head around the fact that there are people on the other side of the glass, real live human beings having emotional moments with the thing that you're putting in their hand and that they're focusing their attention on.
zh: 所以再次说，我认为一旦你真正理解了玻璃对面有真人，正在与你放在他们手中并让他们集中注意力的东西产生情感时刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: You are in those moments.
zh: 你就在那些时刻中。

speaker: Unknown
en: And are you going to own it and show up and be the person you want to be in those moments or not?
zh: 你是要承担它，出现并成为你想在那些时刻成为的人，还是不？

speaker: Unknown
en: A few months ago, I guess a little longer ago, I was talking to the team at Toast who makes the handheld point of sale stuff that they use in restaurants.
zh: 几个月前，我想稍微更早一点，我和 Toast 的团队交谈，他们制造餐厅里使用的手持销售点 stuff。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the thing I was trying to tell them, is whether or not you see it, tonight, you're going to be at dinner with a few 100 000 people all across the country.
zh: 我想告诉他们的事情是，不管你看到没，今晚，你将在全国各地与几十万人一起吃晚餐。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if we take just one example, you're going to be at a very nice diner with a grandmother and her two teenage sons in Ohio, and the check's going to come and the waiter, the waitress is going to hand over the device to that grandmother, because she wants to pick up the bill.
zh: 如果我们只举一个例子，你将在俄亥俄州和一位祖母以及她的两个十几岁的儿子在一家非常好的小餐馆吃饭，账单会来，服务员会把 device 交给那位祖母，因为她想买单。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you have the opportunity to either make her look like a superhero, because she knows what she's doing, or to make her look like a fool and one of her teenage grandsons is going to grab the device and do it for her.
zh: 你有机会让她看起来像个超级英雄，因为她知道自己在做什么，或者让她看起来像个傻瓜，她十几岁的孙子中的一个会抢过 device 为她做这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're at the dinner table, what are you going to do for grandma?
zh: 你就在晚餐桌上，你将为祖母做什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: You going to show up as well as you can, or are you going to just let this whole thing fall apart, because you didn't think hard enough about grandma?
zh: 你要尽可能好地出现，还是你要让这一切崩溃，因为你没有为祖母考虑得足够多？

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's true for Toast, that's true for every product any of us are working on all the time.
zh: 这对 Toast 来说是真的，这对我们要们一直工作的任何产品来说都是真的。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is so interesting and fascinating and inspiring.
zh: 这太有趣了，太迷人了，太鼓舞人心了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was going to ask how you use this insight, that software is kind of the most powerful medium media more than even than TV and movies, and you shared it, which I think is really important.
zh: 我本想问你是如何使用这个洞察的，即软件是一种比电视和电影更强大的媒介 media，而且你分享了它，我认为这真的很重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: So just to kind of double-down on this, is the advice here is think about the emotion you want the user of your software to have as you're starting the design process, not just what do you want them to do, how fast do you want them to get to this flow, it's what's the emotion you want them to have?
zh: 所以为了稍微强调这一点，这里的建议是，在设计过程开始时，考虑你希望你的软件用户有什么样的情感，而不仅仅是你想让他们做什么，你想让他们多快进入这个流程，而是你想让他们有什么样的情感？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I often don't think about what I want them to do.
zh: 我经常不考虑我想让他们做什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: I just think that's sort of a selfish way to think about it.
zh: 我只认为这是一种自私的思考方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: They have something they want to do.
zh: 他们有一些他们想做的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm trying to help them.
zh: 我在试图帮助他们。

speaker: Unknown
en: I just don't ever approach these things of the user's something for me to exploit and take advantage of and manipulate.
zh: 我从不以利用、占便宜和操纵用户的心态来对待这些事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: I know there's people that do approach it that way, which I think is a little unfortunate.
zh: 我知道有些人确实那样对待，我觉得有点不幸。

speaker: Unknown
en: But as a designer, I guess I have my own set of values and my own kind of compass on these things that's pushed me in a certain way of thinking about it.
zh: 但作为设计师，我想我有自己的一套价值观，也有自己在这些事情上的指南针，把我推向了一种特定的思维方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I'm kind of constantly asking what's the right thing for the user?
zh: 所以我不断地问，对用户来说什么是正确的事？

speaker: Unknown
en: And I believe in my heart that if we prioritize that wonderful things will happen for all the metrics, including the money metrics that matter.
zh: 我内心相信，如果我们优先考虑这一点，所有的指标都会产生美妙的结果，包括重要的金钱指标。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've never seen a product be successful that used metrics as a driver for what they were doing.
zh: 我从未见过有哪个产品是靠把指标当作驱动力而取得成功的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've seen a lot of companies be really successfully seeing metrics as a consequence and a way to evaluate the quality of their decisions, and then using those to triangulate and make better decisions moving forward.
zh: 我见过很多公司非常成功，他们是把指标视为结果，并作为评估其决策质量的一种方式，然后利用这些指标进行三角定位，以便在未来做出更好的决策。

speaker: Unknown
en: So they're kind of a very useful feedback mechanism.
zh: 所以它们是一种非常有用的反馈机制。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think there's definitely a risk to confusing, doing something because it's a driver versus something as a consequence.
zh: 但我认为混淆“因为它是驱动力而做某事”和“因为它是结果而做某事”肯定是有风险的。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a few more questions I would ask, but I want to come back to something that I asked earlier, that I think is on the minds of a lot of say founders and product managers listening to this.
zh: 我还有几个问题想问，但我想回到我之前问过的一个问题，我想这也是很多正在听这档节目的创始人和产品经理心中的想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm just like, okay, this all is sounds really great.
zh: 我就像，好吧，这听起来真的很棒。

speaker: Unknown
en: I would love to make these experiences so great.
zh: 我很想把这些体验做得非常棒。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's going to take us a lot of time to do this really, really well.
zh: 要把这些做得真的、真的非常好，会花掉我们很多时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: You said that it doesn't have to.
zh: 你说过这不需要花那么多时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's a tactical tip or two that you can suggest to a founder or product manager to help them contain the design process while also achieving these outcomes that you're describing?
zh: 你能给创始人和产品经理提供一两个战术性的建议，帮助他们在控制设计流程的同时，实现你所描述的这些结果吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, I think if you can give... Maybe one way to think about it is like a big giant AI prompt.
zh: 嗯，我想如果你能给出……也许一种思考方式就像一个巨大的 AI 提示词。

speaker: Unknown
en: The more context you can give it, the more specificity you can give it, the more this is what I'm about and what we're trying to get to, the more the designer's going to be able to figure out which swim lane they're supposed to be in to produce something.
zh: 你能给出的上下文越多，你能给出的具体细节越多，越是说明“我是关于什么的”以及“我们想要达到什么目标”，设计师就越能弄清楚他们应该在哪个泳道里去产出东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think if you're going into it feeling like the design process is going to take a lot of time, it's because you haven't been clear in your creative brief, so to speak, which often means you're not really clear in your own head.
zh: 所以我认为，如果你带着设计流程会花很多时间的感觉进入其中，那是因为你没有在所谓的创意简报中保持清晰，这通常意味着你自己的脑海里也不清楚。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think... I have worked with a lot of founders, and we could identify a bunch of big companies, who I think got started that weren't clear in their own head.
zh: 我认为……我和很多创始人合作过，我们可以列举很多大公司，我认为它们起步时自己脑子里就不清楚。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't want to... Yahoo was an amazing company, but if we just look at Yahoo for a second, I worked there, it was never clear to me what the founding vision of Yahoo was.
zh: 我不想……雅虎是一家了不起的公司，但如果我们要看看雅虎一会儿，我在那里工作过，对我来说雅虎的创始愿景从来就不清楚。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I talk a lot about vision statements and we could say the vision statement of Google is organizing all the world's information.
zh: 我经常谈论愿景声明，我们可以说谷歌的愿景声明是组织全世界的信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a great vision.
zh: 那是一个很棒的愿景。

speaker: Unknown
en: They'll never achieve that.
zh: 他们永远无法实现那个愿景。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's something that's always over the horizon.
zh: 那是总在地平线之外的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's been a very useful organizing principle for their acquisitions and how the company grows.
zh: 而且对于他们的收购和公司的发展方式来说，它一直是一个非常有用的组织原则。

speaker: Unknown
en: Amazon to be the Earth's most customer-centric company.
zh: 亚马逊是成为地球上最以客户为中心的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, great.
zh: 好的，很棒。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a vision, they will never get there.
zh: 那是一个愿景，他们永远无法到达那里。

speaker: Unknown
en: It tells you how they're going to expand.
zh: 它告诉你他们将如何扩张。

speaker: Unknown
en: Apple doesn't have an explicit vision, but I might describe it as personal computing can have a transformative effect on the lives of individuals.
zh: 苹果没有一个明确的愿景，但我可能会把它描述为个人计算可以对个人的生活产生变革性的影响。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that kind of focuses a lot of what they're trying to do.
zh: 我认为这集中体现了他们试图做的大部分事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Disneyland, still the best vision statement of all time, which is the happiest place on earth.
zh: 迪士尼乐园，仍然是历来最好的愿景声明，即地球上最快乐的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: So once you tell an employee this is supposed to be the happiest place on earth, then you're signaling all sorts of things about how they need to pick up the trash and how they need to show up on time and how they need to wear their uniform.
zh: 所以一旦你告诉员工这应该是地球上最快乐的地方，你就在向他们发出关于如何捡垃圾、如何准时出勤以及如何穿着制服等各种事情的信号。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're just signaling a whole bunch of stuff.
zh: 你就是在发出一大堆信号。

speaker: Unknown
en: So when I talked to founders, a lot of times they just don't have that clarity of what's the vision of the company.
zh: 所以当我和创始人交谈时，很多时候他们只是不清楚公司的愿景是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And to go back to Yahoo for a second, I never heard of vision.
zh: 回到雅虎再说一点，我从没听说过愿景。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I'm not really sure what they were ever about.
zh: 所以我不确定他们到底是为了什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: They kind of stumbled into the directory and then they added a bunch of stuff around the edges, but it never seemed to make a lot of sense.
zh: 他们跌跌撞撞地进入了目录，然后他们在边缘添加了一堆东西，但似乎从未有多大意义。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think people operating inside Yahoo, it ended up being inefficient, because they were having to deal with all that ambiguity.
zh: 所以我认为在雅虎内部工作的人，最终变得效率低下，因为他们必须应对所有的模糊性。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think that that can also be a pretty big risk for founders.
zh: 所以我认为这对创始人来说也是一个相当大的风险。

speaker: Unknown
en: They end up caught up with a product idea, and they think that the company is the product, the company is not the product.
zh: 他们最终陷入了一个产品想法，他们认为公司就是产品，但公司不是产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: The product is the product and the company's bigger than the product.
zh: 产品就是产品，而公司比产品更大。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you need to have some vision that speaks beyond just this particular thing.
zh: 你需要有一个超越仅仅这个特定事物的愿景。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think Slack, honestly, both Slack and Pinterest I think are examples of products that became companies, but neither one of those places really knew what to do next, because they didn't have a bigger vision of the change they were trying to see in the world.
zh: 我认为老实说 Slack 和 Pinterest 都是产品变成公司的例子，但这两个地方都不太知道接下来该做什么，因为他们没有关于他们试图在世界上看到的改变的更大愿景。

speaker: Unknown
en: So back to you, you were asking a very pragmatic question.
zh: 言归正传，你问了一个非常务实的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think you need to work on your prompt before you go to your designers and try to give them as much clarity about what you want to produce as possible.
zh: 我认为在去找设计师之前，你需要完善你的提示词，并尽可能给他们关于你想产出什么的清晰度。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think if you leave it open as to the emotional response you want users to have, you're inviting a lot of ambiguity, which is going to invite a lot of inefficiency.
zh: 我认为如果你对希望用户产生的情感反应持开放态度，你就是在邀请大量的模糊性，这将导致大量的低效率。

speaker: Unknown
en: I love that answer.
zh: 我喜欢这个答案。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's so interesting that AI can help us work better together as humans, because when you find that the AI is not achieving the outcome you want as effectively as you want, that's a lesson.
zh: AI 可以帮助我们在人类之间更好地协作，这很有趣，因为当你发现 AI 没有像你希望的那样有效地达到你想要的结果时，那就是一个教训。

speaker: Unknown
en: This also translates the working with humans, make the prompt more specific, add more context in life, not just when you're talking to AI.
zh: 这也转化为与人类共事，让提示词更具体，在生活中添加更多上下文，不仅仅是当你与 AI 对话时。

speaker: Bob Baxley
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I love that.
zh: 我喜欢这个观点。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's so interesting.
zh: 这太有趣了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the advice here is, if you're finding design is taking too long or you want to just level up your success with your design team, give more context, spend more time on the brief, on what you're actually trying to achieve.
zh: 所以这里的建议是，如果你发现设计耗时太长，或者你只是想提升你与设计团队的成功率，就提供更多上下文，在简介上花更多时间，在你真正想要实现的目标上花更多时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: And make sure there's a clear vision or mission that everyone can row towards.
zh: 并确保有一个明确的愿景或使命，让每个人都能够朝着它努力。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Look, design is a problem solving methodology.
zh: 瞧，设计是一种解决问题的方法论。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the more variables you can remove before they go into the process, the more efficient it's going to be.
zh: 所以你能在进入流程之前消除的变量越多，效率就会越高。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you give designers a lot of ambiguity, they're going to spend a lot of time spinning around, and honestly, that's your fault as the client.
zh: 如果你给设计师很多模糊性，他们会花大量时间在此打转，老实说，那是你作为客户的错。

speaker: Unknown
en: As a design leader, I think one of my main challenges is frankly trying to make the PMs better clients, helping them get more specific.
zh: 作为设计负责人，我认为我的主要挑战之一坦率地说是试图让 PM 成为更好的客户，帮助他们变得更具体。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's very common for a design team to get extremely ambiguous asks from a product team.
zh: 设计团队从产品团队那里收到极度模糊的要求是非常普遍的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the problem for designers, they have to take all that ambiguity and they've got to wring it all out.
zh: 对设计师来说，问题在于他们必须接收所有那些模糊性，并且必须将其全部挤榨出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: So when they give it to engineering, engineering knows exactly what to code, because computers don't tolerate ambiguity.
zh: 所以当他们把它交给工程时，工程确切地知道要编码什么，因为计算机不容忍模糊性。

speaker: Unknown
en: Engineers need to know what the thing's going to be.
zh: 工程师需要知道这东西将来是什么样。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so design gets stuck with a really ambiguous input, but they have to have a highly specific output and then often timeboxed to do that.
zh: 所以设计卡在一个真正模糊的输入上，但他们必须有一个高度具体的输出，而且经常有时间限制来做这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's just not a recipe for success.
zh: 这并不是成功的配方。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you're much better off either kind of compressing the PRD experience and bringing the designers into that, kind of co-creating with product and design really rapidly.
zh: 所以你最好要么某种方式压缩 PRD 体验并将设计师带入其中，一种产品与设计真正快速地共同创造的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: But you need to... You could think of it in some ways as designers are going to draw the storyboards, and if you don't give them a great script, they're going to have a very hard time.
zh: 但你需要……你可以从某种角度将其想象为设计师要画分镜脚本，如果你不给他们一个很棒的剧本，他们就会非常艰难。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you can't give the shooting crew ambiguous storyboards or you're just going to waste untold amounts of money on set.
zh: 然后你不能给摄制组模糊的分镜脚本，否则你只是要在片场浪费难以计数的金钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you think about those three steps from script to storyboard to production, it's all about getting rid of ambiguity.
zh: 所以如果你考虑从剧本到分镜再到制作的这三个步骤，那全都是为了消除模糊性。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the more ambiguity that can be removed upstream, the faster design's going to go.
zh: 所以能在上游消除的模糊性越多，设计就会进行得越快。

speaker: Unknown
en: This begs the question then, you don't want to give designers here exactly.
zh: 这就引出了那个问题，那么你不想给设计师……这里。

speaker: Unknown
en: Here's the thing we're designing, make it really great and pretty.
zh: 这就是我们要设计的东西，把它做得非常棒和漂亮。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's always this balance of just give designers space to think and be creative and explore.
zh: 总是存在着这种平衡，既要给设计师空间去思考和发挥创造力及探索。

speaker: Unknown
en: Advice there of just how to navigate that.
zh: 关于如何驾驭这一点的建议。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, if you go back to my example of the script and storyboard, scripts don't contain pictures, there's still a lot of opportunity to think differently and to come up with original things and to have a lot of creative input in the storyboarding process.
zh: 嗯，如果你回到我关于剧本和分镜的例子，剧本不包含图片，仍然有很多机会去不同地思考，去提出原创的东西，并在分镜过程中有很多创造性投入。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the script is living mostly in words, which is largely how PMs function.
zh: 所以剧本主要以文字形式存在，这很大程度上也是 PM 的运作方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: The thing that I will say, to keep in mind for PMs, there's always a tendency on PMs to want to draw something and then try to give a sketch to a designer.
zh: 我想说的，让 PM 记住的一点是，PM 总是有一种倾向想要画点什么，然后试图把草图给设计师。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I would caution them against that.
zh: 我会对此劝诫他们。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sometimes they have to draw themselves so they can think it out.
zh: 有时他们必须自己画出来才能理清思路。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if a PM came to me with something that was drawn and kind of fully baked, my response was like, thanks for giving me that.
zh: 但如果一个 PM 带着画好的东西并且有点完全成熟的东西来找我，我的回应就像这样，谢谢你给我那个。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now I know exactly what we're not going to do.
zh: 现在我确切地知道我们要去做的不是什么了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because as a point of pride, there's no way I'm going to go execute that exact thing.
zh: 因为出于自尊心，我不可能去执行那个确切的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you're right, PMs have to give you the space to operate.
zh: 所以你是对的，PM 必须给你留出操作的空间。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think a lot of what they're trying to achieve could be done in more informal ways, conversationally and whiteboards, things like that.
zh: 我认为他们试图实现的很多东西可以用更非正式的方式完成，通过对话和白板之类的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: But yet you need to narrow the problem for the designers, they need constraints.
zh: 但你需要为设计师缩小问题范围，他们需要约束。

speaker: Unknown
en: They don't need a tiny little box, but they need constraints.
zh: 他们不需要一个小盒子，但他们需要约束。

speaker: Unknown
en: Think in terms of, you don't give them an airport tarmac and you don't even give them a football field.
zh: 想象一下，你不是给他们机场停机坪，你甚至不给他们足球场。

speaker: Unknown
en: You give them something more like a basketball court, a sort of scale at which they can do their design thing.
zh: 你给他们更像篮球场的东西，一种他们可以在其中进行设计工作的规模。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to talk about basketball later, but not yet.
zh: 我想稍后再谈谈篮球，但还不是时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: You've shared a lot of counterintuitive lessons on building product, designing, building teams, leadership.
zh: 你分享了很多关于构建产品、设计、组建团队、领导力的反直觉的经验教训。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is there another very counterintuitive lesson you've learned about building products, hiring leading teams that goes against common startup wisdom?
zh: 还有另一个你学到的关于构建产品、招聘领导团队的非常反直觉的经验教训吗，它违背了常见的创业智慧吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: The thing I would say is that you should wait as long as possible to draw a picture.
zh: 我想说的是，你应该尽可能长时间地等待后再去画图。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that pushes against all the gen AI tools that help you create prototypes.
zh: 我认为这与所有帮助你创建原型的生成式 AI 工具背道而驰。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's obviously a lot of excitement around that.
zh: 显然对此有很多兴奋。

speaker: Unknown
en: I can just give a prompt and the AI, they're going to crank out of UI for me.
zh: 我可以只给一个提示词和 AI，他们会为我生产出一个 UI。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I don't think I'm using the term right, but I had this idea from art that I call the primal mark, and that's the first mark that you make on the canvas.
zh: 所以我不认为我用的术语是对的，但我从艺术中有一个想法，我称之为原始印记，那是你在画布上做出的第一个标记。

speaker: Unknown
en: And once you make that mark on the canvas, everything you do after that is in response to that mark.
zh: 一旦你在画布上做出了那个标记，你在那之后所做的一切都是对那个标记的回应。

speaker: Unknown
en: It sort of sets your baseline.
zh: 它确立了你的基线。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so for me, I always felt that as soon as we drew a picture that looked even remotely real, everybody gravitated towards that and said, oh, that's the thing.
zh: 所以对我来说，我总觉得只要我们画出一幅看起来哪怕有一点点逼真的图，大家就会向它靠拢并说，哦，那就是那东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And people were so uncomfortable with ambiguity that they can't really deal with the tension of, well, that might not be the thing.
zh: 而且人们是如此不适于模糊性，以至于他们无法真正处理那种可能不是那事情的张力。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so as soon as you draw a picture that looks even slightly realistic, much less something that comes out of one of these gen AI tools, everybody kind of goes, oh, that's the thing.
zh: 所以一旦你画出一幅看起来哪怕只是稍微逼真的画，更不用说从这些生成式 AI 工具之一生成的东西，每个人都会有点像那样，哦，那就是那东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: You just keep doubling down on that thing.
zh: 你只会不断在那东西上加倍下注。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what's happened is you've taken the possibilities from this big broad thing down to this tiny little thing from an AI system that's trained on existing solutions and existing ideas and is maybe not even thinking about it the right way, because all you've really given it is your first-order of thinking.
zh: 实际发生的是，你已经把可能性从这个宏大的广阔事物缩减到了这个微小的事物，来自一个在现有解决方案和现有想法上训练的 AI 系统，它甚至可能没有以正确的方式思考，因为你真正给它的只是你的一阶思维。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think there's a way you can stay in these things conceptually and conversationally, where you can get to your second, third, fourth idea.
zh: 我认为有一种方式可以在概念上和对话中保持在这些事物中，这样你可以到达你的第二、第三、第四个想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's where stuff gets really interesting.
zh: 那就是事情变得真正有趣的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: And again, I don't think that has to take a lot of time.
zh: 同样，我不认为那需要花费很多时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: That can be over the course of a single meeting, you could get to a second, third, fourth idea.
zh: 这可能就在一次会议的过程中，你就可以到达第二、第三、第四个想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: You just have to be willing to not jump at the first thing that looks like a possibility.
zh: 你只需要愿意不要跳向第一个看起来像是一个可能性的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: You get that possibility, you go, okay, well that's interesting, let's table that.
zh: 你得到那个可能性，你说，好吧，那很有趣，让我们把它搁置。

speaker: Unknown
en: What else have we got?
zh: 我们还有什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: There's one story that kind of related that's useful.
zh: 有一个相关的故事很有用。

speaker: Unknown
en: In one of my previous jobs, I was responsible for the public website.
zh: 在我之前的一份工作中，我负责公共网站。

speaker: Unknown
en: I remember coming across one of the product managers one day and she's like, "Hey, this link on the home page, we have to make it blue."
zh: 我记得有一天遇到一位产品经理，她说，“嘿，主页上的这个链接，我们必须把它做成蓝色。”

speaker: Unknown
en: I was like, "Well, we don't use blue links anywhere."
zh: 我说，“嗯，我们不在任何地方使用蓝色链接。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And she said, "Yeah, yeah, but we just have to make it blue."
zh: 她说，“是啊，是啊，但我们就是必须把它做成蓝色。”

speaker: Unknown
en: I was like, "Well, we're not making it blue."
zh: 我说，“嗯，我们不会把它做成蓝色。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And a couple of days go by and I saw the home page and the link had been made blue, because she had got around me and she'd gone to engineering and just made it blue.
zh: 过了几天，我看到主页，那个链接被做成蓝色了，因为她绕过了我，她去了工程部门直接把它做成蓝色了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I saw her in the hallway again.
zh: 我又在走廊里看到她。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was like, "What the hell's up with that?"
zh: 我说，“那到底是怎么回事？”

speaker: Unknown
en: And she goes, "Well, people couldn't see it."
zh: 她说，“嗯，人们看不到它。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm like, "Oh, they couldn't see it, so it wasn't prominent enough, right?"
zh: 我说，“哦，他们看不到它，所以它不够显眼，对吗？”

speaker: Unknown
en: She's like, "Yeah, it wasn't prominent enough."
zh: 她说，“是的，它不够显眼。”

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm like, "Well, great.
zh: 我说，“嗯，很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a 100 different things we could do to make it more prominent, one of which is making it blue, which is the thing that came to you first because you're not a designer, it's naturally... Because it's the most obvious thing, but it actually doesn't fit in with these larger things we're trying to do."
zh: 我们有一百种不同的方法可以让它更显眼，其中一种是把它做成蓝色，这是首先出现在你脑海中的东西，因为你不是设计师，这很自然…… 因为它是最显而易见的东西，但它实际上并不符合我们要做的这些更大的事情。”

speaker: Unknown
en: So I've often... I try to encourage the product managers to what's the problem with the thing?
zh: 所以我经常…… 我试着鼓励产品经理去搞清楚那东西的问题是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: And then let us solve it.
zh: 然后让我们来解决它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Don't jump to it and tell us... Don't tell us this is just exactly what we're supposed to do.
zh: 不要跳向它并告诉我们…… 不要告诉我们要做的正好就是那个。

speaker: Unknown
en: And again, I do the same thing on the roadmap.
zh: 同样，我在路线图上也做同样的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: You decide the roadmap, tell us what we're supposed to do, I will ask you about it, and I may push back and we may have some back and forth, but that's your responsibility.
zh: 你决定路线图，告诉我们应该做什么，我会问你，我可能会反驳，我们可能会有一些来回，但那是你的责任。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm going to trust that you are trained and you know what you're doing and you're going to make the right call.
zh: 我会相信你是受过训练的，你知道你在做什么，你会做出正确的决定。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I just want you to give me the same level of respect.
zh: 我只希望你能给我同样的尊重程度。

speaker: Unknown
en: This advice about not drawing quickly and not making that primal mark, which I love that term, is, I'm curious your take on AI prototyping tools these days.
zh: 关于不要快速作图和不要做那个原始标记的建议，我很喜欢那个术语，我很好奇你对现在的 AI 原型工具的看法。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because that's the extreme version of that.
zh: 因为那是那事情的极端版本。

speaker: Unknown
en: Not only are you just creating a sketch, it's like, oh, it's working, here it is.
zh: 你不仅在创建草图，而是像，哦，它在运行，在这里。

speaker: Unknown
en: Here's what it looks like.
zh: 这就是它的样子。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thoughts on that, do you discourage people from doing that, PMs especially?
zh: 对此有什么想法，你会不鼓励人们这样做吗，尤其是 PM？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, I think it's a production tool.
zh: 嗯，我认为它是一个生产工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: Once you know what you want and you can give it a really robust prompt, then... I haven't played with it a lot myself, because I'm not in an operational role right now, but presumably it's really useful at cranking out that actionable prototype which you can click and experience.
zh: 一旦你知道你想要什么，并且你可以给它一个非常稳健的提示词，那么…… 我自己没有怎么玩过它，因为我现在不是在运营角色，但据推测它在生成那个可点击和体验的可操作原型方面非常有用。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I've said for a long time that an interactive idea needs to be expressed interactively, so we're not talking with our hands and we can really understand what's going to happen.
zh: 我很久以前就说过，一个交互式的想法需要交互式地表达，所以我们不是用手说话，我们可以真正理解将会发生什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: So when the idea is ready to be expressed, I think those tools are probably fantastic.
zh: 所以当想法准备好被表达时，我认为那些工具可能棒极了。

speaker: Unknown
en: But ideas start off pretty fragile, and the best ideas start off really fragile.
zh: 但想法开始时相当脆弱，最好的想法开始时真的非常脆弱。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think when you push them to develop too quickly and you put them out in the world and expect them to be able to stand up to critique too early, you're just going to squash them.
zh: 我认为当你推动它们发展得太快，并把它们推向世界，并期望它们能够太早地经受批评时，你只会把它们扼杀。

speaker: Unknown
en: I often think about them like the little plant in the Pixar movie, Wall-E, you've got to give that little guy a little space, a little time, some water and some nourishment, and you can't really just suddenly put him out in the wind and think he's going to make it.
zh: 我经常像皮克斯电影《机器人总动员》(Wall-E) 里的那株小植物一样想它们，你必须给那个小家伙一点空间，一点时间，一些水和一些营养，你不能真的只是突然把他放在风中并认为他会挺过去。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think a lot of... There's a lot of very fragile, interesting, quiet ideas that I think you need to give some space.
zh: 所以我认为有很多…… 有很多非常脆弱的、有趣的、安静的想法，我认为你需要给它们一些空间。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when you jump to the expression of them, I think you're putting them at risk.
zh: 当你跳到它们的表达时，我认为你是在让它们冒风险。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'll also say that, everybody, when they look at a prototype, what they're focusing on is the visual and textual expression.
zh: 我还要说，每个人，当他们看原型时，他们关注的是视觉和文字表达。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so as soon as you produce something in high resolution the feedback you're going to get is going to be about colors and shapes and these presentation layer things, which are very loosely related to usability and value.
zh: 所以一旦你生产出高分辨率的东西，你得到的反馈将是关于颜色和形状以及这些表现层的东西，它们与可用性和价值关系非常松散。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like focusing on the special effects of a movie that has a really bad story.
zh: 这就像关注一部故事非常糟糕的电影的特效。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so at ThoughtSpot, we used to use what we call block brain diagrams, which were even simplified versions of wire frames.
zh: 所以在 ThoughtSpot，我们过去常使用我们称之为块脑图的东西，这甚至比线框图更简化。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was just big chunky blocks of here's how the screen could be and where things might be located.
zh: 那只是大块的区域，这是屏幕可能的样貌以及事物可能位于何处。

speaker: Unknown
en: And because it was so low fidelity, people couldn't get into commenting on what it looked like.
zh: 而且因为它是如此低保真，人们无法去评论它看起来怎么样。

speaker: Unknown
en: We had to talk about conceptually what it was.
zh: 我们不得不从概念上讨论它是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we were trying to build up this firm foundation where we could go from the block frames to wire frames to kind of the final expression.
zh: 所以我们试图建立这个坚实的基础，我们可以从块图到线框图再到最终的表达。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think it helped us clarify what we were trying to do conceptually so that by the time we got to the final visual presentation, that stuff was actually really simple.
zh: 我认为这帮助我们在概念上阐明了我们试图做的事情，以至于当我们到了最终的视觉呈现时，那些东西实际上真的很简单。

speaker: Unknown
en: And initially it made the product team really nervous because we would be sitting in these block frames and wire frames for sometimes weeks, and they'd be like, when are we finally going to see the comps?
zh: 起初这让产品团队非常紧张，因为我们有时会花上几周时间坐在这些块图和线框图前，他们会说，我们什么时候终于能看到合成稿？

speaker: Unknown
en: And then what would happen, is because we had such a robust design system, once we locked down on the block frames, we could send it to an agency and they could do the full high-res comps in a day, because they knew exactly what they were doing.
zh: 然后发生的事情是，因为我们有如此强大的设计系统，一旦我们确定了块图，我们就可以把它发给代理机构，他们可以在一天内完成全套的高清合成稿，因为他们确切地知道自己在做什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the PMs were always like, what the hell happened overnight?
zh: 所以产品经理总是说，这到底一夜之间发生了什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: You're like, well, it turns out that the high-res stuff, that's not the hard thing.
zh: 你会觉得，嗯，结果是高清的东西，那不是难事。

speaker: Unknown
en: The hard thing is the heavy lifting of thinking, what are we really trying to do?
zh: 困难的部分是思考的重活，我们到底想做什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: That's the hard part.
zh: 那才是难的部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you do the high-res stuff, you really muddy the waters.
zh: 如果你做高清的东西，你真的会把水搅浑。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think you end up spending a lot more time churning, if you didn't... Again, I'm going to go back to the movie metaphor, because I studied film.
zh: 我认为如果你没有……我要再次回到电影的比喻，因为我学过电影。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you're trying to fix script issues when you're in production or storyboarding, you're going to churn and you're going to waste a lot of effort.
zh: 如果你在拍摄制作或分镜阶段试图解决剧本问题，你会陷入空转，你会浪费很多精力。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you've got to figure out what you're trying to do before you go draw the high-res stuff.
zh: 所以你必须弄清楚你想做什么，然后再去画高清的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think a lot of the gen AI tools, it's this seductive thing of, hey, let's just go, let's go make the comp and see what we think.
zh: 我认为很多生成式 AI 工具都有这种诱惑，嘿，我们就直接去做合成稿，看看我们怎么想。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't really know if you're going to get anything great out of that process, maybe.
zh: 我真的不确定你是否能从那个过程中得到什么伟大的东西，也许吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a really interesting counter-narrative because it feels like every team now is just straight to prototypes.
zh: 这是一个非常有趣的反面叙事，因为感觉现在每个团队都是直接进入原型。

speaker: Unknown
en: I just had the C... She's one of the CPOs at Microsoft.
zh: 我刚跟那位 C……她是微软的首席产品官之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: I realize there's many CPOs, and she has this concept of demos before memos and just prompt sets or any PRDs, you should just be prototyping all your ideas.
zh: 我意识到有很多首席产品官，她有一个概念叫备忘录前的演示，在任何提示词集合或产品需求文档之前，你应该只是把你所有的想法原型化。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it's interesting to hear the perspective of maybe it's actually hurting your ability to come up with a really clever solution versus the obvious solution.
zh: 所以听到这种观点很有趣，也许这实际上在削弱你提出一个真正聪明的解决方案而不是显而易见的解决方案的能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Look, I think at some point, hopefully people just back up and ask themselves, are we actually producing better product because of this process?
zh: 听着，我认为在某种程度上，希望人们只是退一步问自己，因为这个过程，我们真的在制造更好的产品吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And we're going faster, but faster can't be the ultimate goal.
zh: 我们走得更快了，但更快不能是最终目标。

speaker: Unknown
en: You need to be creating something great as well, right?
zh: 你也需要创造一些伟大的东西，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Something that's sustainable and frankly that you're proud of and your users find value in.
zh: 一些可持续的东西，坦率地说，那是你引以为豪的，并且你的用户能从中找到价值的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you're just throwing so much spaghetti at the wall, I don't know if having a spaghetti throwing machine that goes faster is...
zh: 如果你只是在墙上扔太多的意大利面，我不确定拥有一台扔得更快意大利面的机器是否是……

speaker: Unknown
en: Look, there's a counter argument that's... You can say, oh, it's like Darwinian evolution, and we're just going to spin through a bunch of random mutations and see what happens.
zh: 听着，有一个反驳论点是……你可以说，哦，这就像达尔文进化论，我们只是要经历一堆随机突变，看看会发生什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I used to joke that it's true, that if you take a bunch of hydrogen atoms and give them 14 billion years, you could end up with a tiger, but you don't know you're going to get a tiger and you could get a six headed shrimp instead, and you don't really know when it's going to shift.
zh: 我过去常开玩笑说这是真的，如果你拿一堆氢原子并给它们 140 亿年，你最终可能会得到一只老虎，但你不知道你会得到一只老虎，你可能反而得到一只六头的虾，而且你真的不知道它什么时候会转变。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I'm not exactly sure Darwinian evolution is the way we create great product, but a lot of companies are making a run at it.
zh: 所以我不确定达尔文进化论是我们创造伟大产品的方式，但很多公司都在尝试这样做。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to take us to a recurring segment on the podcast called AI Corner.
zh: 我想带我们进入播客上的一个常设环节，叫 AI 角落。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in AI Corner, I ask guests to share what's one way that you've learned or figured out to use AI in your job to help you do better work, to help you do faster work?
zh: 在 AI 角落，我请嘉宾分享一种你学到或发现的方法，在你的工作中使用 AI 来帮助你做得更好，帮助你做得更快？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, my job right now is trying to figure out what my job is.
zh: 嗯，我现在的工作是试图弄清楚我的工作是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the thing I've been using AI for is I've very explicitly been using it as a life coach.
zh: 所以我一直用 AI 做的事情是，我非常明确地把它用作生活教练。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I had seen a couple of prompts about asking it what a blind spot was or what my strengths and weaknesses were.
zh: 所以我看过一些关于询问它盲点是什么或者我的优缺点是什么的提示词。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'd seen some prompts about that stuff.
zh: 我看过一些关于那些东西的提示词。

speaker: Unknown
en: And one of them was really fantastic.
zh: 其中一个真的很棒。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of them was, what's an outdated mindset that I'm holding onto that's not still serving me?
zh: 其中一个是，我坚持的一个过时心态是什么，它已经不再对我有益了？

speaker: Unknown
en: And it came back with a very polite prompt or very polite response about, well, given your age and your profession, it's not surprising that you're very wedded to the idea of control, but that's not really the world we're living in anymore.
zh: 它带回了一个非常有礼貌的提示词或者非常有礼貌的回应，关于，嗯，考虑到你的年龄和职业，你对控制这个想法非常执着并不令人惊讶，但这不再是我们要生活的世界了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's not probably going to suit the thing you're trying to do next, which is writing and publishing and speaking and stuff.
zh: 而且这可能不适合你接下来想做的事情，也就是写作、出版和演讲之类的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And although it's statistically derived, it did come back with a really nice phrase, which I view...
zh: 虽然它是统计推导出来的，但它确实带回了一个很好的短语，我认为……

speaker: Unknown
en: Although it's statistically derived, it did come back with a really nice phrase which I've used in your show, which was, try to focus on choreography over control.
zh: 虽然它是统计推导出来的，但它确实带回了一个很好的短语，我在你的节目中用过，那就是，试着专注于编排而不是控制。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I thought that was really useful.
zh: 所以我认为那真的很有用。

speaker: Unknown
en: I asked for some of my blind spots, that was also useful.
zh: 我询问了我的一些盲点，那也很有用。

speaker: Unknown
en: I use it for a lot of exercise input, that's useful.
zh: 我用它来做很多运动输入的辅助，那很有用。

zh: 所以我要推荐的三本书，第一本是一本关于排版的美妙诗意的书，叫《排版风格要素》，作者是 Robert Bringhurst。

en: Robert was the poet laureate of Canada.

en: And the first 80 pages will change how you think about typography.

en: It will open you up to the wonderful world of typography that we all live in.

en: It's just a very interesting collection of impressionistic views of time and how time passes and what time means.
zh: 这只是一个非常有趣的印象派观点的集合，关于时间、时间如何流逝以及时间意味着什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's very different from the others and it's not something probably gets recommended on your show too often, but I think it'll help people in their lives in a powerful way.

en: So that's super fascinating and then I'll throw one other in there, which is not something I've recently seen, but something I highly recommend for everybody, which is Lords of Arabia.

speaker: Unknown
en: The Lords of Arabia is I think one of the two or three best expressions of the medium of film.
zh: 《阿拉伯的劳伦斯》我认为是电影媒介最好的两三个表现之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so when you think about the ability to hold moving pictures, characters, story, music, photography, set design, costume, the whole constellation of variables that come to play into a movie, I think Lords of Arabia is probably one of the two or three most complete expressions of what the medium is capable of.
zh: 所以当你考虑承载动态画面、角色、故事、音乐、摄影、布景设计、服装、所有这些变量汇聚在一起发挥作用的能力时，我认为《阿拉伯的劳伦斯》可能是该媒介能力的最完整的两三个表现之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think it's useful to think about in technology, all the different elements of a product and all the different elements of a user interface and how you can break those down the way you can break down all these elements of a movie and how many pieces of software do we use where somebody is actually conducting that symphony in a really coherent, powerful, full on way.
zh: 我认为在技术领域思考它很有用，思考产品的所有不同元素和用户界面的所有不同元素，以及你可以如何像分解电影的所有这些元素那样分解它们，以及我们使用多少软件有人真的在以一种真正连贯、强大、全面的方式指挥那场交响乐。

speaker: Unknown
en: I love that movie.
zh: 我爱那部电影。

zh: 你专注于最近，我只是要反驳一下。

en: No, there's nothing terribly recent.
zh: 不，没有什么非常近期的。

en: The stuff that I go back to, I'll give you a couple of nerdy ones.

zh: 我总是谈论徕卡相机，它们贵得离谱，但徕卡相机的问题在于当你用徕卡拍摄时，你的表现会不同。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 所以当人们想到相机时，他们想到的是图像质量，他们不会想到工具将如何改变他们。

speaker: Unknown
en: When you show up with an iPhone, you're thinking about sharing.

zh: 当你带着数码单反出现时，你只是拍一堆照片并希望会有一些结果。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think these cameras are very useful metaphor for being conscious about how the tools you pick are going to impact the thing that you produce.
zh: 所以我认为这些相机是非常有用的隐喻，用于有意识地意识到你选择的工具将如何影响你生产的东西。

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: And then the software product I would point out, which is not terribly new, but I think it's worth noting, is a tool called Habitica.

speaker: Unknown
en: And Habitica is really fascinating.
zh: Habitica 真的非常迷人。

en: Ultimately, it's a habit tracker and task management app, but it's fundamentally a game.
zh: 归根结底，它是一个习惯追踪器和任务管理应用，但它根本上是一个游戏。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a role playing game where you create a character and your character revolves and can buy armor and go on quests and things as you check off your habits and stuff.
zh: 它是一个角色扮演游戏，你创建一个角色，你的角色会演变，可以购买护甲，去探险，当你勾选你的习惯和东西时。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 这是我见过的最有趣的概念模型转换的表现。

en: So these are different genres.
zh: 所以这些是不同的流派。

speaker: Unknown
en: And Habitica is really interesting because it mixes genres, it mixes role playing game with to do manager.
zh: Habitica 真的很有趣，因为它混合了流派，它混合了角色扮演游戏和待办事项管理器。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think it's a really powerful example of how you can really shift the user's thinking in the same way movies for example.
zh: 所以我认为这是一个非常强大的例子，说明你可以如何真正改变用户的思考，就像例如电影那样。

speaker: Unknown
en: Star Wars is ultimately a cowboy movie set in space.

en: And when you come to those two genre mashups are really interesting.

en: If somebody suddenly got shot in a rom-com, that would not make sense to you in the same way that if somebody made a really funny joke in a John Wick movie, it wouldn't make sense.

en: So I think Habitica is just the most interesting example I've ever found is somebody really doing a fascinating mashup of conceptual models, which is... Sorry, I'll stop.

en: It's an unexplored and unexploited possibility of software ideas.
zh: 这是一个未被探索和未被利用的软件想法的可能性。

en: I love how profound this lightning round already is.
zh: 我很喜欢这个闪电问答环节已经变得如此深刻。

en: The point about Leica changing the way you even think about the photo is so interesting, I've never thought of it that way.

zh: 这是真的，他们可以走得更快。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we live in a time when it's very easy to produce things at incredibly high production values, but they don't mean anything.
